- **Key historical events:** 1820–1850 coincides with early industrialization in western Massachusetts and the War of 1812 pension period; both affect which records survive

## Boundary changes
- Berkshire County was formed in 1761 from Hampshire County. Its external boundaries remained stable throughout 1820–1850.
- Records for events before 1761 fall under Hampshire County, not Berkshire.
- No sub-county reorganizations affected civil record-keeping during the target period.

---

## Available record types

For this period, Massachusetts kept vital records at the **town level** — not at the county level. Every birth, marriage, and death question routes to the town clerk of the specific town where the event occurred, not to a county office.

### Vital records (civil registration)

- **Town-level registration (1639 onward):** The FamilySearch Massachusetts Vital Records wiki (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Massachusetts_Vital_Records) states that recording of births, marriages, and deaths was ordered as early as 1639, though not all places complied consistently. The original record is held by the clerk of the town or city where the event occurred.
- **State-level registration (from 1841):** The same wiki page states Massachusetts was the first state to create a permanent statewide recording system, starting in 1841. For 1820–1840, there is no statewide registry — town clerks are the only civil source. From 1841 onward, state copies also exist, held by the Massachusetts Registry of Vital Records and Statistics.
- **Marriage intentions:** Per the Massachusetts Vital Records wiki, intentions were commonly recorded in the bride's home town, with additional copies sometimes appearing in the groom's home town and their current residence. A marriage that crossed a town line may appear in two separate sets of registers.
- **Published series:** The wiki_search result at https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Massachusetts_Genealogy#Colonial notes that "Published compilations include the 'Vital Records of [Town Name] to 1850' series for over 200 towns." Many Berkshire towns are included. Confirm whether the specific town has a published volume before turning to original registers — these books are widely held in public libraries and by the New England Historic Genealogical Society (NEHGS).
- **FamilySearch (name-indexed):** Collection 2061550, "Massachusetts, Town Vital Records, 1620-1890" — 3,456,789 records, free, searchable by name with images at https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/2061550. This is the primary online starting point.
- **FamilySearch (browse-only):** Volume 004500891 — Town Clerk Vital and Town Records, Berkshire County, 1761–1850 — 512 images, 0% name-indexed, not full-text searchable. Must be browsed image by image with no name search.
- **Gaps:** Births are the most unevenly recorded event type before 1841. Not all Berkshire towns complied consistently before the state system began.

### Church records

- **Importance:** Because civil registration was town-level and compliance was uneven before 1841, church baptism and burial entries may be the only documentation for many vital events in this period.
- **Record types:** Baptisms, marriages, burials, confirmations, and membership rolls.
- **FamilySearch (name-indexed):** Collection 1921657, "Massachusetts, Church Records, 1630-1920" — 987,654 records, free at https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1921657.
- **FamilySearch (browse-only):** Volume 004500892 — Church Records (Congregational), Pittsfield, 1791–1850 — 274 images, 0% name-indexed, not full-text searchable. Browse-only; covers only the Congregational congregation in Pittsfield.
- **Gaps:** The browse-only digitized volume covers Pittsfield Congregational records only. Records for Baptist, Methodist, Episcopal, Quaker, and rural congregations outside Pittsfield are not confirmed as digitized in this survey.
- **Other repositories:** Non-digitized church records may be held by individual congregations, the Congregational Library (Boston), appropriate denominational archives, or the NEHGS (https://www.americanancestors.org/), which the FamilySearch wiki identifies as "the largest genealogical library in the region" (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Massachusetts_Genealogy#Military).
- **Language:** English.

### Census records

- **Federal census:** The 1820, 1830, 1840, and 1850 federal censuses all cover Berkshire County. The 1820, 1830, and 1840 enumerations name only the head of household; other family members are tallied by age bracket and sex. The 1850 census is the first to list every household member by name and age, making it the anchor year for family reconstruction.
- **Mortality schedule:** The 1850 census introduced a separate mortality schedule listing deaths in the preceding year — a valuable substitute for civil death records.
- **State census:** Massachusetts did not conduct a regular state census during 1820–1850. No state enumeration fills the intercensal gaps in this period.
- **Access:** Federal censuses are name-indexed at Ancestry (https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/census/, subscription) and at FamilySearch (free).

### Probate and court records

- **Types:** Wills (testate estates), letters of administration (intestate estates), estate inventories, guardianship appointments, and petitions. Filed at the county level at the Berkshire County Probate Court in Pittsfield.
- **Date range:** From county formation in 1761; for events before 1761, search Hampshire County probate.
- **FamilySearch (name-indexed):** Collection 1678901, "Massachusetts, Probate Records, 1635-1991" — 567,890 records, free at https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1678901.
- **Originals:** Berkshire County Probate Court, Pittsfield.

- **Survey system:** Metes and bounds — the New England system based on natural landmarks and compass bearings. No rectangular/township-range system applies.

The Massachusetts Archives (Boston) — identified by the FamilySearch Massachusetts Genealogy wiki (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Massachusetts_Genealogy#Colonial) as holding original colony records — also holds state-level militia and service records.

- **Online coverage:** Find A Grave (https://www.findagrave.com/) indexes many Berkshire County cemeteries by name.
- **Physical records:** Sexton records and burial registers are held by individual towns and congregations. The Berkshire Athenaeum (Pittsfield Public Library) and local historical societies may hold transcriptions.

- **Local papers:** Pittsfield had local newspapers during this period. Exact titles and founding dates are not confirmed by any tool result returned in this survey — do not rely on a specific name without independent verification.

# Locality Guide: Billy Civil Parish, County Antrim, Ireland (1780–1870)

> **Survey note:** The FamilySearch place-resolution tools returned no results for any Ireland jurisdiction (County Antrim, Billy civil parish, etc.), and every Ireland-specific FamilySearch Wiki page attempted redirected to a generic US fallback rather than Ireland content. The one exception was the **Ireland Naming Customs** page, which returned real content and is fully cited below. All other sections honestly report the tool gap and direct you to consult those resources directly in a browser.

---

## Jurisdiction Overview

The Billy civil parish lies within County Antrim in the historic province of Ulster, in the northeast of Ireland. Because the place-resolution tools returned no data for any Ireland jurisdiction, specific details on formation dates, population figures, denominational composition, and boundary history could not be retrieved from the survey tools.

**Recommended next steps for jurisdiction context:**
- Open **https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/County_Antrim,_Ireland_Genealogy** directly in a browser (the survey tool redirected this URL to a generic page)
- Open **https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Genealogy** directly

---

## Boundary Changes

No tool data was returned. Consult the FamilySearch Wiki's County Antrim page (URL above) for administrative and boundary history.

---

## Available Record Types

Each section below notes which FamilySearch Wiki page covers the topic. All were attempted in the survey; all returned generic fallback content. Access them directly in a browser.

### Vital Records (Civil Registration)
- **Page to consult:** https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Vital_Records
- Civil registration of births, marriages, and deaths did not begin in Ireland until 1864 (non-Catholic marriages from 1845). Records before that date must be found in church registers, land records, and other substitutes.

### Church Records
- **Page to consult:** https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records
- County Antrim had a mix of Church of Ireland (Anglican), Presbyterian, Roman Catholic, and smaller Nonconformist congregations. Parish registers of baptisms, marriages, and burials are the primary pre-1864 substitutes for civil registration.

### Census Records
- **Page to consult:** https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Census
- Irish census records before 1901 are largely destroyed (1861 and 1871 censuses were pulped; 1821–1851 returns were mostly lost in the 1922 Public Record Office fire). Census substitutes — Tithe Applotment Books (1823–1837) and Griffith's Valuation (1847–1864) — are the key enumerative sources for the target period.

### Land Records
- **Page to consult:** https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Land_and_Property
- **Tithe Applotment Books (1823–1837):** List landholders liable for tithes; cover most of County Antrim.
- **Griffith's Primary Valuation (1847–1864):** The closest thing to a census substitute for mid-19th century Ireland; names every householder and landholder in each townland.
- **Estate papers and rent rolls:** Significant for the 1780–1830 period before the Tithe Books.

### Probate and Court Records
- **Page to consult:** https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Probate_Records
- Pre-1858 probate was handled by ecclesiastical courts (Prerogative Court of Armagh for larger estates; Consistorial Court of Down and Connor for County Antrim). Most original wills were destroyed in 1922; will calendars and abstracts survive.

### Military Records
- No tool data returned. Researchers should check the FamilySearch Wiki for Ireland Military Records and the National Archives of Ireland.

### Cemetery Records
- No Ireland-specific cemetery database links were returned. Try the **CWGC** (Commonwealth War Graves Commission), **IrishGraveyards.ie**, and **Find A Grave** for County Antrim coverage.

### Newspaper Records
- No tool data returned. The **British Newspaper Archive** and the **Irish Newspaper Archives** are key repositories for County Antrim newspapers in this period.

### Immigration / Emigration Records
- Significant emigration from County Antrim occurred throughout 1780–1870, especially during the Famine decade (1845–1852). Passenger manifests at arrival ports (Liverpool, New York, Philadelphia, Quebec) are the primary records. When examining a manifest, check all household members — infants and children traveling with parents are listed.

---

## Repository Guide

The survey tools returned 0 FamilySearch collections and 0 digitized volumes for County Antrim. This is a tool coverage gap — it does not mean no FamilySearch material exists for this area. Key repositories to consult directly:

| Repository | What it holds | URL |
|---|---|---|
| **Public Record Office of Northern Ireland (PRONI)** | Church registers, estate papers, valuation records, wills | https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/proni |
| **National Archives of Ireland (NAI)** | Tithe Applotment Books, Griffith's Valuation, census fragments | https://www.nationalarchives.ie |
| **General Register Office (GRO), Dublin** | Civil registration from 1864 | https://www.gro.ie |
| **FamilySearch Catalog** | Microfilmed parish registers and county records | https://www.familysearch.org/search/catalog |
| **Ancestry (Ireland collections)** | Griffith's Valuation, civil registration indexes, census substitutes | https://www.ancestry.com |

**Search the FamilySearch Catalog** directly for "Billy" and "Antrim" — the catalog may hold microfilmed parish registers and other County Antrim material not surfaced by the survey tools.

---

## Known Record Losses

- **1922 Public Record Office fire** (Dublin): Destroyed the vast majority of 19th-century census returns (1821, 1831, 1841, 1851) and a large proportion of pre-1858 wills and original probate records.
- **Census destruction**: The 1861 and 1871 Irish censuses were deliberately destroyed by government order; the 1881 and 1891 returns were pulped during World War I.
- **Church records**: Some parish registers were lost before deposit, particularly Catholic registers from the late 18th and early 19th centuries.

---

## Research Tips: Irish Naming Customs

The only Ireland-specific FamilySearch Wiki page that returned substantive content in this survey was **Ireland Naming Customs** (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Naming_Customs). Its key points for researching Billy civil parish, 1780–1870:

### Surnames
- Irish Gaelic surnames were commonly **anglicized**, producing many spelling variants. The same family may appear as O'Flynn, Flynn, and Flinn; O'Houlihan may appear as Holland.
- The prefixes **Mac** (son of) and **O** (grandson/descendant of) were frequently dropped or restored over time. Always search with and without these prefixes.
- Spelling was not standardized; one family's surname may be recorded several different ways within one parish.

### Given Names
- Irish given names were also anglicized, producing variants that can look unrelated — Darby, Dermot, and Jeremiah are cited by the FamilySearch Wiki as variations of the same name.
- Some given names were used for **both males and females** (the Wiki cites Florence, Sydney, and Evelyn). Do not assume sex from a given name alone.
- Nicknames may little resemble the formal name used in official records.

### Traditional Naming Pattern

A traditional pattern was often followed by Irish parents in this period:

| Birth order | Usually named for |
|---|---|
| First son | Father's father |
| Second son | Mother's father |
| Third son | The father himself |
| Fourth son | Father's eldest brother |
| First daughter | Mother's mother |
| Second daughter | Father's mother |
| Third daughter | The mother herself |

> The FamilySearch Wiki states explicitly: *"The pattern is a clue, not a rule — it was not universally followed, and a broken pattern is not evidence of non-identity."* Use it to generate candidate relative names, not to exclude identities.

---

## Summary

The survey tools were unable to resolve any Ireland place names or retrieve Ireland-specific FamilySearch Wiki content for County Antrim or Billy civil parish (all pages returned a generic US-focused fallback). The naming customs from the FamilySearch Wiki are the only tool-sourced Ireland content in this guide.

**Practical priorities for a researcher working this parish in 1780–1870:**
1. Griffith's Primary Valuation (1847–1864) — the closest census substitute
2. Tithe Applotment Books (1823–1837) — landholders, pre-Famine
3. Church registers at PRONI — baptisms, marriages, burials before 1864 civil registration
4. Civil registration indexes from 1864 — births, marriages, deaths
5. Open the FamilySearch Wiki pages for Ireland and County Antrim directly in a browser — the survey tools could not access them but they likely hold digitization status and additional repository detail

| Third son | The father himself |
| Fourth son | Father's eldest brother |
| First daughter | Mother's mother |
| Second daughter | Father's mother |
| Third daughter | The mother herself |

## Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania — Locality Research Guide (1840–1880)

**County background:** Schuylkill County has existed continuously since 1811. The period 1840–1880 covers the peak of the anthracite coal boom, heavy immigration (Irish, Welsh, German, and Eastern European), and rapid industrialization.

### Records Found on FamilySearch

| Record Type | Date Range | Status | Notes |

# Locality Guide: Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania (1840–1880)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Formed:** 1811 (place_search dateRange "+1811/"; parent jurisdictions not stated in tool results)
- **County seat / administrative center:** Not confirmed by tool results
- **Parent jurisdiction:** Pennsylvania, United States
- **Population during period:** No data returned by place_population for this county and period
- **Economy:** Not confirmed by tool results (FamilySearch Wiki returned only generic content)
- **Ethnic composition:** Not confirmed by tool results
- **Religious denominations:** Volume 007936751 carries both English and German language records (1842–1895), indicating English- and German-speaking congregations were present
- **Key historical events:** Not confirmed by tool results

## Boundary changes
- Schuylkill County has been in continuous existence since 1811 (place_search dateRange "+1811/"). No boundary changes within the 1840–1880 target period are indicated by tool results. If the county was formed from Berks and/or Northampton Counties, pre-1811 records may reside in those parent counties — consult the FamilySearch Wiki directly to confirm the formation history.

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)
- **Start date:** Not confirmed — the FamilySearch Wiki returned only generic content for all Pennsylvania-specific pages during this survey; the researcher must consult https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Pennsylvania_Vital_Records directly for the level (town, county, or statewide) and year civil registration began. The generic page notes many U.S. states did not require statewide registration until the early 1900s.
- **What exists:** FamilySearch digitized volume 007936753 covers Schuylkill County marriage records 1870–1910 (94 images, browse-only, 0% indexed). No birth or death registration volumes for the 1840–1880 period appeared in volume_search results.
- **Gaps:** No birth or death volumes appear for the target period. Marriage coverage starts only in 1870 (volume 007936753); the 1840–1869 marriage window has no confirmed online source.
- **Pre-registration alternatives:** Church records (baptism, marriage, burial registers — see below)

### Church records
- **Denominations present:** Not specified in tool results; English- and German-speaking congregations are evidenced by the bilingual volume 007936751
- **Record types:** Baptisms, marriages, burials (standard church register content; not confirmed specifically by tool results)
- **Where held:** FamilySearch digitized volume 007936751 (Church Records 1842–1895, 187 images, browse-only, 0% indexed, English and German). FamilySearch collection SYNTH-PA-CHURCH ("Pennsylvania, Schuylkill County Church Records (synthetic test fixture)," 1708–1985, 1,245,830 records, 982,415 persons, 607,220 images) — note: this collection is labeled "synthetic test fixture" in the tool result and must be verified before citation.
- **Gaps:** Volume 007936751 is browse-only with no name indexing; German-language records require reading in German. Pre-1842 church registers for the county have no confirmed online presence in tool results.
- **Language:** English and German (volume 007936751)

### Census records
- **Federal census:** The 1840, 1850, 1860, 1870, and 1880 federal censuses would cover Schuylkill County. Ancestry collection 1276 ("1850 United States Federal Census - Schuylkill County," https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/1276/) was returned by external_links_search. The generic FamilySearch Wiki page notes mortality schedules recorded deaths in the year preceding each decennial census (1850–1885).
- **State census:** Not confirmed by tool results
- **Other enumerations:** Not confirmed by tool results
- **Access:** Ancestry (collection 1276) provides indexed access to the 1850 census. No FamilySearch census volumes for Schuylkill County appeared in volume_search results for 1840–1880; the 1860, 1870, and 1880 enumerations would typically be available on FamilySearch and Ancestry but were not returned in the external_links_search.

### Probate and court records
- **Types:** Wills, estate inventories, letters of administration, guardianship files
- **Date range:** FamilySearch collection 1999196 ("Pennsylvania, Probate Records, 1683–1994") covers the target period; FamilySearch volume 007936749 covers Schuylkill County probate records 1851–1930 (412 images)
- **Where held:** FamilySearch collection 1999196 (3,200,560 images, 0 indexed records — browse-only); volume 007936749 (0% name-indexed, not full-text searchable — must be browsed image by image). Originals are at the county courthouse and/or state archives (not confirmed by tool results).

### Land records
- **Survey system:** Not confirmed by tool results
- **Land-distribution jurisdiction:** Not confirmed by tool results; FamilySearch Wiki returned only generic content
- **Types:** Deed records confirmed by volume 007936752 (1815–1900, 543 images, 22% name-indexed)
- **Where held:** FamilySearch volume 007936752 — roughly 22% of images are searchable by name; the remaining ~78% must be browsed. County Recorder of Deeds holds originals.

### Military records
- **Relevant conflicts:** Mexican-American War (1846–1848), Civil War (1861–1865) fall within or adjacent to the target period
- **Record types:** The generic FamilySearch Wiki page notes service records, pension files, bounty land warrants, and draft registrations at the National Archives; state adjutant general records may be at the Pennsylvania State Archives
- **Where held:** NARA (Philadelphia or Washington, DC); Pennsylvania State Archives (specifics not confirmed by tool results)

### Cemetery records
- **Major cemeteries:** Not confirmed by tool results
- **Online coverage:** FindAGrave and BillionGraves were not listed in external_links_search results for this period
- **Physical records:** Sexton records held at individual cemeteries (not confirmed by tool results)

### Newspaper records
- **Local papers:** Not confirmed by tool results
- **Where held:** Not confirmed by tool results; local historical society and state library are typical repositories
- **Content value:** Obituaries, marriage notices, and legal notices (typical value; not confirmed specifically for this county in tool results)

### Immigration/emigration records
- **Relevant ports:** Not specified for Schuylkill County in tool results
- **Record types:** FamilySearch volume 007936750 covers Schuylkill County naturalization records 1849–1915 (298 images, browse-only, 0% indexed). The generic FamilySearch Wiki page states pre-1906 naturalizations can appear in any court of record.
- **Where held:** FamilySearch (volume 007936750); NARA for passenger lists and post-1906 naturalizations
- **Content note:** Passenger lists (arrival manifests) record every person aboard, including infants and young children traveling with parents. When researching a family, examine the full manifest for all family members — children as young as newborns are listed.

### Tax records
- **Types:** Ancestry collection 7667 ("Pennsylvania, U.S., Tax and Exoneration Lists, 1768–1801," https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/7667/) was returned by external_links_search but predates the 1840–1880 target period
- **Date range:** No tax record collections or volumes for 1840–1880 appeared in tool results
- **Where held:** Physical county and state repositories for the target period (not confirmed by tool results)
- **Substitute value:** Tax lists can substitute for missing census years

### Other record types
- No school, institutional, organizational, or occupational record collections appeared in tool results for this period

## Repository guide

### Online repositories
| Repository | Collections for this place | Gap it fills | Access |
|---|---|---|---|
| FamilySearch | Collection 1999196 "Pennsylvania, Probate Records, 1683–1994" (3.2M images, browse-only); Volume 007936751 Church Records 1842–1895 (187 images, browse-only); Volume 007936752 Deed Records 1815–1900 (543 images, 22% indexed); Volume 007936750 Naturalization Records 1849–1915 (298 images, browse-only); Volume 007936753 Marriage Records 1870–1910 (94 images, browse-only) | Probate, church, land, naturalization, post-1870 marriages | Free |
| Ancestry (collection 1276) | "1850 United States Federal Census - Schuylkill County" (https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/1276/) | 1850 census; gap in FamilySearch census coverage | Subscription |

**Coverage of this survey:** The volume_search returned all 5 matching digitized volumes for Schuylkill County — the result set is complete (no nextPageToken, totalResults = 5).

### Physical repositories
| Repository | Holdings | Access method |
|---|---|---|
| Schuylkill County Courthouse / Recorder of Deeds | Land records, court records, probate originals | In-person / mail |
| Pennsylvania State Archives | State-level records, military adjutant general records | In-person / online request |
| NARA (Philadelphia or Washington, DC) | Federal census originals, military service and pension records, naturalization records | In-person / online request |
| Local historical and genealogical societies | Transcriptions, cemetery surveys, manuscript collections | Contact society directly |

## Records NOT online
- Birth and death records for the 1840–1880 period did not appear in any volume or collection returned by tool results
- Marriage records before 1870 (volume 007936753 starts 1870) have no confirmed online source
- Church register images before 1842 (pre-volume 007936751) have no confirmed online source
- Tax records for the 1840–1880 period did not appear in tool results
- Military service and pension records are held at NARA; online access depends on the specific record and platform
- The FamilySearch Catalog was not searchable during this survey (tool unavailable); additional microfilm and manuscript holdings may exist there

## Known record losses
No tool result confirmed any specific record destruction for Schuylkill County in the 1840–1880 period. An empty search result is a coverage gap, not confirmed loss. Contact the Schuylkill County Courthouse and the Pennsylvania State Archives to confirm the status of any record class before concluding records do not exist.

## Research tips
- The FamilySearch Wiki returned only generic fallback content for all Pennsylvania- and Schuylkill County-specific pages during this survey. Consult https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Pennsylvania_Vital_Records, https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Schuylkill_County,_Pennsylvania_Genealogy, and https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Pennsylvania_Church_Records directly before building a research plan — these pages may contain specific dates, repositories, and indexing details not captured here.
- Church records in volume 007936751 include German-language entries; the researcher must read German to use those records effectively.
- Pre-1906 naturalization records can appear in any court of record. Volume 007936750 (Naturalization Records 1849–1915, browse-only) must be browsed image by image with no name search; plan significant time for this.
- Deed records volume 007936752 (1815–1900, 22% indexed) offer partial name-search capability — run a name search first, then browse the unindexed portion for ancestors active in land transactions during 1840–1880.
- The 1850 census for Schuylkill County is available on Ancestry (collection 1276, https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/1276/); the 1860, 1870, and 1880 federal censuses were not returned by tool results but would typically be available on FamilySearch and Ancestry — search those platforms directly.
- The FamilySearch Catalog (catalog_search) was not available during this survey. Search it manually at familysearch.org/catalog for "Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania" to identify microfilm rolls, manuscript collections, and finding aids not captured in this guide.

output.text_response:
# Locality Guide: Billy Civil Parish, County Antrim, Ireland (Bushmills Area), 1780–1870

---

## Jurisdiction Overview

- **Civil parish:** Billy, Barony of Dunluce, County Antrim, Province of Ulster
- **Nearest town:** Bushmills (north Antrim coast)
- **Period governance:** Part of the United Kingdom from 1800 (Acts of Union). After 1922, County Antrim became part of Northern Ireland; records devolved to PRONI and GRONI.
- **Religious composition:** Church of Ireland and Presbyterian (majority Protestant, descended from 17th-century plantation settlers), Roman Catholic (indigenous Irish), with smaller Methodist/dissenting congregations. In 1861, the census recorded ~60% Protestant, ~40% Catholic in Northern Ireland generally.

---

## Key Fact for the Period: No Civil Registration Until 1864

Before civil registration began on **1 January 1864**, church registers are the **only** systematic source for births (baptisms), marriages, and burials. For 1864–1870 (the tail of the target period), civil records exist at GRONI.

---

## Church Records — The Core Source

### Church of Ireland (Anglican)

- Registers began as early as 1536 in Ireland, but **two-thirds were destroyed in the 1922 Public Record Office fire** in Dublin.
- Whether the Billy/Bushmills Church of Ireland registers survived must be checked against:
  - **RCB Library parish register list:** https://www.ireland.anglican.org/cmsfiles/pdf/AboutUs/library/registers/ParishRegisters/PARISHREGISTERS.pdf
  - **PRONI's digitized church records portal (free):** https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/articles/digitised-church-records-available-proni#toc-1
- Surviving registers are held at **PRONI** (Belfast) and/or the **Representative Church Body (RCB) Library** (Dublin).
- Marriage proxy records also survive in the **Ireland Diocesan and Prerogative Marriage License Bonds Indexes, 1623–1866** (FamilySearch collection 3460239; also Ancestry, MyHeritage, FindMyPast) — these are independent of the parish registers and survived 1922.
- FindMyPast holds the **Ffolliott Collection** (CoI baptisms, marriages, burials) and Betham/Crossle/Thrift genealogical abstracts of records destroyed in 1922.

> **Bottom line:** Establishing whether Billy's Church of Ireland registers survived 1922 is the first research task. Check the RCB Library list and PRONI's portal before assuming they are gone.

### Roman Catholic

- Irish Catholic registers generally begin from the mid-1700s; **most rural parishes did not start until Catholic Emancipation in 1828.** Expect records for the Bushmills area to begin around 1828 or shortly after, possibly with earlier fragments.
- Catholic registers were **not** held at the PRO Dublin in 1922 and were **not** destroyed. They are essentially intact.
- Available free at the **National Library of Ireland:** https://registers.nli.ie/
- Also indexed with images at **Ancestry** (Ireland, Catholic Parish Registers, 1655–1915) and **RootsIreland.ie** (subscription).

### Presbyterian

- Many registers began around 1830 (average starting date for north Ulster). The Bushmills area had significant Presbyterian population from plantation-era Scottish settlement.
- Registers held at **PRONI**, many digitized.
- Also indexed by the **Ulster Historical Foundation:** http://www.ancestryireland.com/
- FindMyPast holds Ireland Non-Conformist records.

---

## Census Records — Largely Destroyed

| Census Year | Fate |
|---|---|
| 1821, 1831, 1841, 1851 | Mostly destroyed in the 1922 PRO Dublin fire; fragments survive |
| 1861, 1871, 1881, 1891 | **Officially destroyed** (deliberately pulped — not a fire loss) |
| 1901, 1911 | Complete; free at census.nationalarchives.ie (post-target-period) |

**For the target period, Tithe Applotment Books and Griffith's Valuation are the census substitutes.**

---

## Land Records — The Census Substitutes

| Record | Years | Coverage | Access |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Tithe Applotment Books** | 1823–1837 | All landholders (all denominations — Catholic, Presbyterian, CoI all paid tithes) | Free: titheapplotmentbooks.nationalarchives.ie; also FamilySearch |
| **Griffith's Primary Valuation** | ca. 1860–1864 for Antrim | Every property occupier with landlord | Free: askaboutireland.ie/griffith-valuation/; also FamilySearch |
| **Estate rentals and papers** | Ongoing throughout period | Tenant families named generation by generation | PRONI (Belfast) — physical or ordered copies |
| **Registry of Deeds (Dublin)** | From 1708 | Landholders who registered deeds | In-person at Registry of Deeds, Dublin; microfilm at FamilySearch |

---

## Civil Registration (1864–1870 only)

- Births, marriages (all denominations), and deaths from 1 January 1864.
- **Where held:** General Register Office for Northern Ireland (GRONI), Oxford House, 49–55 Chichester Street, Belfast BT1 4HL.
- Indexes from 1864 searchable free at **IrishGenealogy.ie**.

---

## Probate Records

- Before 1858: ecclesiastical probate (Diocese of Connor and Down for County Antrim). Most originals destroyed in 1922.
- After 1858: civil probate district system. County Antrim records at **PRONI**.
- Surviving indexes: **Ireland, Indexes to Wills, Probate Administration, Marriage Bonds and Licences, 1591–1866** (Ancestry); Betham, Crossle, and Thrift genealogical abstracts at FindMyPast preserve content from records destroyed in 1922.

---

## Other Important Record Types

| Type | Coverage | Where Held |
|---|---|---|
| **National School registers** | From 1831; name pupils with birth years and parents | PRONI |
| **Poor Law records** (Ballymoney Poor Law Union) | Famine era and after; workhouse admissions | PRONI |
| **Newspapers** (Belfast News-Letter from 1737; Coleraine Chronicle from 1844) | Obituaries, marriage notices, emigration notices | British Newspaper Archive (subscription); Linen Hall Library (Belfast) |
| **Military records** (British Army, Napoleonic Wars onward) | Service and pension records for County Antrim soldiers | The National Archives (UK), Kew; indexed on Ancestry/Findmypast |
| **RIC (Royal Irish Constabulary) records** | From 1836 | The National Archives (Kew); PRONI; also Ancestry/FamilySearch |
| **Graveyard inscriptions** | Various dates | North of Ireland Family History Society; FindAGrave |
| **Trade directories** (Pigot's, Slater's) | Merchants and householders in Bushmills from 1820s | National Library of Ireland; Linen Hall Library |

---

## Repository Quick Reference

| Repository | Access | URL / Contact |
|---|---|---|
| **PRONI** (Public Record Office of Northern Ireland), Belfast | Free digitized records online; in-person or copy service | nidirect.gov.uk/proni |
| **RCB Library** (Dublin) | In-person; paid search service | ireland.anglican.org/library |
| **GRONI** (Belfast) | In-person; certified copies | nidirect.gov.uk/groni |
| **National Library of Ireland** | Catholic registers free online | registers.nli.ie |
| **National Archives of Ireland** | Tithe books free online; 1901/1911 census free | nationalarchives.ie; titheapplotmentbooks.nationalarchives.ie |
| **The National Archives (UK), Kew** | British Army/RIC records | nationalarchives.gov.uk |
| **FamilySearch** | Marriage bonds index; Tithe books; Griffith's; Catholic registers | familysearch.org |
| **Ancestry** | Catholic registers; CoI records; military; probate indexes | ancestry.com (subscription) |
| **RootsIreland.ie** | North-of-Ireland church record indexes | rootsireland.ie (subscription) |
| **Ulster Historical Foundation** | Presbyterian/CoI and emigration databases | ancestryireland.com (subscription) |
| **FindMyPast** | Ffolliott Collection; non-conformist records; Betham/Thrift abstracts | findmypast.com (subscription) |
| **British Newspaper Archive** | Ulster newspapers | britishnewspaperarchive.co.uk (subscription) |

---

## Known Record Losses

- **1922 PRO Dublin fire:** Destroyed two-thirds of all-Ireland Church of Ireland parish registers, most pre-1858 probate records, and most 1821–1851 census returns.
- **Deliberate census destruction:** 1861, 1871, 1881, 1891 returns pulped by official order.
- **Substitute strategy:** Tithe Applotment Books + Griffith's Valuation replace the missing census for 1823–1864; estate rentals at PRONI fill the 1780–1823 gap for tenants on the great north Antrim estates.

---

## Recommended First Steps

1. **Check Church of Ireland register survivorship** for Billy civil parish via the RCB Library list and PRONI's portal before assuming any register is gone.
2. **Identify the specific church congregation(s)** serving Billy civil parish using PRONI's *Guide to Church Records* (https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/sites/default/files/publications/Guide-to-Church-Records-October-2019.pdf) — civil parish boundaries and church parish boundaries do not align exactly.
3. **Pull the Tithe Applotment entry** for your family's townland (free online) to establish a pre-Famine household.
4. **Pull the Griffith's Valuation entry** to establish the household around 1860 and identify the landlord.
5. **Search Catholic registers** at NLI's free portal (registers.nli.ie) for the relevant Catholic parish — Catholic families in this area were not destroyed by 1922 and registers are largely intact from around 1828.
6. **Search Ulster Historical Foundation and RootsIreland.ie** for indexed church records that may not yet appear on Ancestry or FamilySearch.

---

# Locality Guide: Billy Civil Parish, County Antrim, Ireland (Bushmills Area) (1780–1870)

## Jurisdiction overview

- **Administrative level:** Billy is a civil parish in the Barony of Dunluce, County Antrim, in the historic province of Ulster.
- **County seat / administrative centre:** Antrim town; the nearest town to Billy civil parish is Bushmills on the north Antrim coast.
- **Parent jurisdiction:** County Antrim, Province of Ulster, Ireland (part of Great Britain throughout the target period under the Acts of Union 1800). After 1922, County Antrim became part of Northern Ireland, United Kingdom.
- **Population during period:** Population figures for this civil parish were not returned by any tool during this survey. The 1821, 1831, 1841, and 1851 censuses were conducted for all-Ireland; survivorship is addressed under Census records below.
- **Economy:** North Antrim in this period was predominantly agricultural, with smallholder tenant farming, some linen industry, and fishing along the coast near Bushmills. The Giant's Causeway made the area a destination from the early 19th century.
- **Ethnic composition:** The area reflects the Ulster Plantation of the early 17th century. The population was mixed Protestant (Church of Ireland and Presbyterian, descended from Scottish and English settlers) and Catholic (largely indigenous Irish-speaking communities).
- **Religious denominations:** Church of Ireland (Anglican), Presbyterian (several congregations), Roman Catholic, with smaller Methodist and other dissenting congregations. The Ireland_Church_Records wiki page states that in Northern Ireland, "the Church of Ireland and various aspects of the Presbyterian Churches were the dominant religions, accounting for sixty-percent of the population in 1861. While Catholics were a minority, they accounted for forty-percent of the population." [https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records]
- **Key historical events:** The 1798 United Irishmen's Rebellion affected Ulster. The Acts of Union 1800 merged Ireland into the United Kingdom. The Great Famine (1845–1852) caused severe population loss in County Antrim, though less devastatingly than in western counties, and triggered heavy emigration. The target period (1780–1870) ends just after civil registration began.

## Boundary changes

- Billy civil parish boundaries were set before the target period and were stable throughout it.
- For record-keeping purposes, the relevant administrative unit above the civil parish was County Antrim, whose records are now held at the Public Record Office of Northern Ireland (PRONI) in Belfast.
- County Antrim fell under all-Ireland institutions (General Register Office, Public Record Office Dublin) until 1922, when it became part of Northern Ireland; its records then devolved to PRONI and the General Register Office for Northern Ireland (GRONI). The Ireland_Church_Records page states: "Copies of many national records up to 1922 are available in both the NAI [National Archives of Ireland] and PRONI and similarly registration records in GRO and GRONI. Records after 1922 are held in their respective offices." [https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records]

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)

- **Start date:** The Ireland_Church_Records wiki page states explicitly: "Before civil registration was introduced in 1864, Church records provide the primary source for providing baptism, marriage and burial dates." Civil registration of births, marriages, and deaths for all Ireland began on 1 January 1864. For the vast majority of the target period (1780–1863), there are no civil vital records — church registers are the only systematic vital record source.
- **What exists for the tail of the period (1864–1870):** Births, marriages (all denominations), and deaths registered with civil registrars from 1864.
- **Where held:** General Register Office for Northern Ireland (GRONI), Oxford House, 49–55 Chichester Street, Belfast BT1 4HL. Index searches and certified copies are available via GRONI. Indexes from 1864 are also searchable via IrishGenealogy.ie.
- **Gaps:** None in the civil registration series from 1864 onward, but under-registration of births and deaths was common in the early years. The target period gives only six years of civil records (1864–1870).
- **Pre-registration alternatives:** Church registers (baptisms, marriages, burials) for all denominations are the essential substitute — see Church records below.

### Church records

This is the most critical record class for the entire 1780–1870 window. The specific denominations present in and around Billy civil parish need to be confirmed via PRONI's Guide to Church Records (https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/sites/default/files/publications/Guide-to-Church-Records-October-2019.pdf), which, per the Ireland_Church_Records wiki page, identifies what churches exist in each parish, what records exist, and whether those records are held at PRONI. No tool result in this survey returned the specific congregation names or register dates for Billy civil parish; use the PRONI Guide to establish them.

**Church of Ireland (Anglican/Episcopalian)**
- The Ireland_Church_Records page states: "Church of Ireland Records began in 1536, but two-thirds were destroyed in 1922. This was the religion of many of the Northern Ireland London Company plantation settlers in the 17th century." [https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records]
- This is directly applicable to the Billy/Bushmills area, which is plantation-era settlement territory.
- Surviving registers are held at PRONI (Belfast) and/or at the Representative Church Body (RCB) Library (Braemor Park, Churchtown, Dublin 14; library@ireland.anglican.org). A list of surviving Church of Ireland parish registers with their locations is published by the RCB Library: https://www.ireland.anglican.org/cmsfiles/pdf/AboutUs/library/registers/ParishRegisters/PARISHREGISTERS.pdf
- PRONI has digitized many of its church records, available at: https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/articles/digitised-church-records-available-proni#toc-1
- Registers that survived 1922 and are held at PRONI are available free of charge via PRONI's online portal.
- Online indexes for some Church of Ireland baptisms, marriages, and burials appear on the FindMyPast Ffolliott Collection (subscription): Irish Parish Register Baptisms & Confirmations, Marriages, and Burials.
- The Ireland Diocesan and Prerogative Marriage License Bonds Indexes, 1623–1866 (FamilySearch collection 3460239; also at MyHeritage and FindMyPast) is a proxy-marriage source surviving outside the parish registers.
- **Gap:** Two-thirds of Church of Ireland registers across all of Ireland were destroyed in the 1922 Public Record Office fire in Dublin. Whether the specific registers for Billy's Church of Ireland congregation survived must be checked against the RCB Library list and PRONI holdings.

**Roman Catholic**
- The Ireland_Church_Records page states: "Ireland Catholic Church Records began from the mid 1700s. Most rural parishes did not start keeping records until Catholic Emancipation in 1828." North Antrim was a rural area; Catholic registers for the Bushmills area likely begin around 1828 or shortly after, with possible earlier fragmentary entries.
- Catholic registers were NOT destroyed in the 1922 fire as they were held locally by parishes, not at the PRO Dublin.
- Catholic registers for County Antrim are available via the National Library of Ireland's free online microfilm portal: https://registers.nli.ie/
- Also indexed (with images) at Ancestry: Ireland, Catholic Parish Registers, 1655–1915 (subscription).
- The RootsIreland.ie index (subscription) covers many Catholic registers for the north of Ireland.
- **Language:** Catholic registers in this period are typically in Latin or English.

**Presbyterian**
- The Ireland_Church_Records page states: "In 1605 Scottish estate owners resettled mostly Presbyterian tenants from their estates to newly established estates in Northern Ireland. Numerous registers date from the 1600s, but the average starting date for these registers is 1830." Presbyterian records for the Bushmills area may therefore start around or after 1830.
- Presbyterian registers for Northern Ireland are held at PRONI. PRONI has digitized many of these.
- The Ulster Historical Foundation (http://www.ancestryireland.com/) indexes Presbyterian and other north-of-Ireland church records.
- FindMyPast holds Ireland Non-Conformist Births & Baptisms, Burials, Congregational Records, and Marriages (subscription).

**Methodist and Other Dissenting Congregations**
- A Methodist society began in Dublin in 1746; congregations existed in Ulster from mid-18th century.
- FindMyPast holds Ireland Non-Conformist records (subscription).
- **Language:** All Protestant registers in English.

### Census records

- **Irish census survivorship is a critical issue.** The 1861, 1871, 1881, and 1891 census returns for all of Ireland were officially destroyed (not lost in 1922, but deliberately pulped). The 1821, 1831, 1841, and 1851 returns were mostly destroyed in the 1922 PRO Dublin fire, though fragments survive.
- **What remains:** The 1901 and 1911 census returns (both post-target-period) are complete and freely available at the National Archives of Ireland (census.nationalarchives.ie). For the target period, almost no original census household schedules survive for County Antrim.
- **Surviving fragments and substitutes:** Census search forms and fragments from 1841 and 1851 were sometimes preserved as part of pension applications and are held at PRONI. Griffith's Primary Valuation (1847–1864) and the earlier Tithe Applotment Books (1823–1837) are the main population-substitute surveys for the target period — see Tax records below.
- **Access:** The 1901 and 1911 census returns, not strictly within the target window but the earliest complete survivals, are free at census.nationalarchives.ie.

### Probate and court records

- **Probate:** Testamentary records before 1858 were handled by the Church of Ireland consistorial courts (diocesan probate). After 1858, a civil probate district system was introduced. County Antrim fell under the Diocese of Connor and Down for pre-1858 ecclesiastical probate.
- Indexes to wills and administrations were published in various compilations. Many pre-1922 original wills were destroyed in the 1922 fire. Surviving indexes include: Ireland, Indexes to Wills, Probate Administration, Marriage Bonds and Licences, 1591–1866 (Ancestry, subscription). Betham Genealogical Abstracts, Crossle Genealogical Abstracts, and Thrift Genealogical Abstracts at FindMyPast preserve abstracts of records destroyed in 1922.
- Post-1858 wills for County Antrim are held at PRONI (which holds the northern district's probate records).
- **Where held:** PRONI holds surviving probate records for County Antrim from the 1858 civil probate system onward. Pre-1858 survivals are fragmentary and scattered across surviving indexes and abstracts.

### Land records

- **Land records are the most important substitute sources for census gaps in the target period.**
- **Tithe Applotment Books (1823–1837):** Landholders in each civil parish (Protestant, Catholic, and Dissenter alike) were surveyed to assess liability for tithes paid to the Church of Ireland. This is a household-by-household survey covering Billy civil parish in the 1820s–1830s. Available free at the National Archives of Ireland (titheapplotmentbooks.nationalarchives.ie) and on FamilySearch.
- **Griffith's Primary Valuation (1847–1864):** A comprehensive survey of all property holders in Ireland. County Antrim was surveyed in the early 1860s. Names every occupier of land or property, with landlord names. Freely searchable at AskAboutIreland.ie (https://www.askaboutireland.ie/griffith-valuation/) and at IrishOrigins.net (subscription). Also on FamilySearch.
- **Estate papers and rentals:** The great landed estates of north Antrim (including the Antrim estate, the Londonderry estate, and others) kept their own rental records and maps. These are held at PRONI and are a rich source for 1780–1870, often naming tenant families generation by generation.
- **Registry of Deeds (Dublin):** Deeds and mortgages involving land were registered in Dublin from 1708. These abstract-indexes survive and cover 1780–1870 for County Antrim landholders who chose to register deeds. The index is available on microfilm through FamilySearch.
- **Survey system:** Metes and bounds, not rectangular survey. Land was measured in townlands (the basic Irish land division), then civil parish, then barony, then county.
- **Where held:** Tithe and Griffith records free online; estate papers at PRONI; Registry of Deeds records at the Registry of Deeds, Dublin (and microfilmed by FamilySearch).

### Military records

- **Relevant conflicts:** The United Irishmen's Rebellion (1798), the Napoleonic Wars (service in British army, 1793–1815), and later Victorian-era service.
- **Record types:** British Army service records and pension files are held at The National Archives (UK), Kew (service records, muster rolls, Chelsea Pensioners records). Many muster rolls and pension records for soldiers from County Antrim are available via Findmypast and Ancestry (British army records, subscription). The Ireland_Church_Records page references the National Archives; for Irish servicemen in the British Army, The National Archives (Kew) is the primary repository.
- **Militia records:** County Antrim had a militia; militia records are at PRONI.
- **PRONI** also holds some local military records and muster rolls for County Antrim militia.
- The FamilySearch Wiki page for Ireland Military Records returned only a generic fallback page in this survey — that page should be consulted directly at https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Military_Records when the wiki is accessible.

### Cemetery records

- **Major cemeteries:** Church of Ireland graveyards (attached to parish churches), Catholic churchyards, and Presbyterian meeting-house graveyards exist throughout the Bushmills area. Ballycastle, Ballintoy, and Bushmills areas have historic graveyards.
- **Online coverage:** FindAGrave (findagrave.com) and the Irish Gravestone Inscriptions project cover some north Antrim graveyards. The North of Ireland Family History Society has published graveyard surveys for County Antrim.
- **Physical records:** Graveyard inscription surveys may be held at PRONI or at the North of Ireland Family History Society.

### Newspaper records

- **Local papers:** The Ballymena Observer, the Coleraine Chronicle (from 1844), and the Belfast News-Letter (from 1737, the oldest surviving English-language newspaper in Ireland) covered north Antrim. Obituaries, marriage notices, land auction notices, and legal notices appear in these papers.
- **Where held:** The British Newspaper Archive (britishnewspaperarchive.co.uk, subscription) holds digitized runs of many Ulster papers. The Linen Hall Library (Belfast) and PRONI hold microfilmed local newspapers. The Belfast Telegraph archive is available via some subscription services.
- **Content value:** Obituaries (especially for wealthier or notable residents), marriage announcements, Famine-era emigration notices, and estate sale notices.

### Immigration/emigration records

- **Scale and significance:** North Antrim experienced significant emigration throughout this period, especially post-Famine (1845–1855). Many emigrants went to North America (particularly Canada and the eastern United States).
- **Passenger lists:** Pre-1820 passenger lists are sparse. After 1820, US passenger arrival manifests survive at NARA and are indexed on Ancestry and FamilySearch. Canadian arrivals are at Library and Archives Canada.
- **Ulster emigration records:** The Ulster Historical Foundation (http://www.ancestryireland.com/) specializes in north-of-Ireland emigration research. Some emigration lists and notices survive in estate papers at PRONI.
- **Naturalization records:** US naturalizations from before 1906 were filed in any court of record; NARA holds federal court naturalizations.
- **Content note:** Passenger lists record all persons aboard including infants and children traveling with parents. When researching a family, examine the full manifest for all members.

### Tax records

- **Tithe Applotment Books (1823–1837):** The most important tax-substitute census for the pre-Famine period. Names all tithe-liable landholders in each civil parish. Free at titheapplotmentbooks.nationalarchives.ie and on FamilySearch.
- **Griffith's Primary Valuation:** As noted under Land records — covers 1847–1864 and names every property occupier. Free at AskAboutIreland.ie.
- **Hearth Money Rolls (1660s):** An earlier tax list naming householders; fragmentary survivals for County Antrim exist and have been published.
- **Substitute value:** Tithe Applotment and Griffith's together effectively replace the destroyed census returns for 1823–1864.

### Other record types

- **School records:** National Schools were established in Ireland from 1831 under the National Board of Education. School registers naming pupils (including birth years and parents' names) survive for many County Antrim schools and are held at PRONI. These are important for 1831 onward.
- **Directories:** Pigot's, Slater's, and other Irish trade directories from the 1820s onward name merchants and substantial householders in towns including Bushmills. Available at the National Library of Ireland and reprinted in various publications.
- **Poor Law records:** The Poor Law Union for the Bushmills area was Ballymoney Poor Law Union. Workhouse records (admission registers, minute books) are at PRONI and can name individuals in dire circumstances during the Famine era.
- **Constabulary records:** The Royal Irish Constabulary (from 1836) kept station records; RIC records are held at The National Archives (Kew) and PRONI. The RIC register (naming officers by county of birth) is on Ancestry and FamilySearch.

## Records NOT online

- Original Church of Ireland parish registers held at PRONI that have not yet been digitized — check PRONI's current digitization list before assuming a register is available online.
- PRONI estate papers and rental records (indexed but images require in-person viewing or copies ordered from PRONI).
- Poor Law Union records (Ballymoney Poor Law Union records for the Bushmills area) — at PRONI, not fully digitized.
- County Antrim militia and constabulary records — at PRONI and The National Archives (Kew), mostly physical only.
- Local town and parish directories pre-1840 — held at Linen Hall Library and National Library of Ireland.

---

## Known record losses

- **The 1922 Public Record Office fire in Dublin** destroyed a large portion of Church of Ireland parish registers held there for safekeeping, as well as many pre-1858 probate records and substantial portions of the 1821, 1831, 1841, and 1851 census returns. The Ireland_Church_Records wiki page states that "two-thirds [of Church of Ireland records] were destroyed in 1922." [https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records] Whether the specific Church of Ireland registers for Billy civil parish survived depends on whether they had been deposited in Dublin before 1922 — this must be checked against the RCB Library's surviving register list.
- **Census returns for 1861, 1871, 1881, 1891** were officially destroyed (not lost in a disaster). No tool result in this survey confirmed the fate of the 1821–1851 County Antrim returns; the general pattern for all of Ireland is that they were destroyed in the 1922 fire. Griffith's Valuation and Tithe Applotment Books are the principal substitutes.
- **Substitute sources:** Tithe Applotment Books (1823–1837); Griffith's Primary Valuation (ca. 1860–1864 for County Antrim); estate rentals at PRONI; and Betham/Crossle/Thrift genealogical abstracts of destroyed probate records.

---

## Research tips

- **Church of Ireland registers are the first record class to establish for any family in Billy civil parish.** Because County Antrim was plantation territory, many families were Church of Ireland for centuries before the target period. Check the RCB Library's parish register list (https://www.ireland.anglican.org/cmsfiles/pdf/AboutUs/library/registers/ParishRegisters/PARISHREGISTERS.pdf) and PRONI's digitized records (https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/articles/digitised-church-records-available-proni#toc-1) before assuming the register for your parish did not survive the 1922 fire.
- **Know the civil parish, townland, and church parish distinctly.** Civil parishes (the administrative unit for Tithe Applotment and Griffith's) do not align exactly with Catholic parish boundaries or Church of Ireland parish boundaries. A family in Billy civil parish may have worshipped in a church parish that extends into adjoining civil parishes. PRONI's Guide to Church Records (https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/sites/default/files/publications/Guide-to-Church-Records-October-2019.pdf) maps church congregations to civil parishes.
- **Tithe Applotment (1823–1837) names heads of household paying tithes — Catholics, Presbyterians, and Church of Ireland alike** (tithes supported the Church of Ireland regardless of the payer's own faith). Use it as a census substitute for the 1820s–1830s.
- **Griffith's Primary Valuation** (ca. 1860 for County Antrim) is the best single name-list for the mid-period. Cross-reference with church baptism registers to extend family relationships back before 1847.
- **Search across denominational lines.** The Ireland_Church_Records wiki page advises: "Search available Church of Ireland records even if your family was not of the Church of Ireland" and "Search surrounding localities if you cannot find records in the expected locality." [https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records] In the Bushmills area, Catholic families are sometimes found in Church of Ireland burial registers, and vice versa.
- **The Ulster Historical Foundation** (http://www.ancestryireland.com/) and **RootsIreland.ie** (http://www.rootsireland.ie/) specialize in north-of-Ireland research and index records not yet on Ancestry or FamilySearch — check both for County Antrim church and emigration databases.

**Quirk — FamilySearch Wiki partially unreachable during this survey:** Only the Ireland_Church_Records page returned full content; all other Ireland-specific pages (Civil Registration, Census, Land and Property, Probate, Military, Presbyterian Church Records, Getting Started, Research Tips) returned a generic fallback. Re-run the locality guide or check those pages directly at familysearch.org/en/wiki before relying on their absence.

---

Billy civil parish is in north County Antrim near the Bushmills coast, and the 1780–1870 window falls almost entirely before civil registration, which did not begin in Ireland until 1864. For most of these ninety years, church registers — Church of Ireland (Anglican), Presbyterian, and Roman Catholic — are the only systematic sources for births, marriages, and deaths. Two-thirds of Church of Ireland registers were destroyed in a 1922 fire in Dublin, so the first task is to check whether Billy's church records survived; those that did are held at the Public Record Office of Northern Ireland (PRONI) in Belfast and the Representative Church Body Library in Dublin, with many now free online through PRONI's digital portal. Where registers are missing, the Tithe Applotment Books (1820s–1830s) and Griffith's Primary Valuation (ca. 1860) substitute for the missing census records, since the Irish census returns for 1861 and 1871 were officially destroyed and earlier returns were lost in the 1922 fire. The most important warnings for this research are the 1922 destruction of Church of Ireland registers (check survivorship before assuming a register is gone), the misalignment between civil and church parish boundaries (identify the specific congregation, not just the civil parish), and the need to search all three denominational streams in an area where Church of Ireland, Presbyterian, and Catholic families lived side by side.

The next step is to confirm which specific church congregations served Billy civil parish using PRONI's Guide to Church Records, then check whether their registers survived and are online or must be ordered from PRONI or the RCB Library.

# Locality Guide: Billy Civil Parish, County Antrim, Ireland (1780–1870)

## Jurisdiction Overview

- **Location:** Northern County Antrim, centered on the market town of Bushmills; formerly the head of an ecclesiastical union (with Armoy, Ballyclug, Donegore, and Kilbride).
- **Barony:** Partly Carey, chiefly Lower Dunluce; Poor Law Union of Coleraine.
- **Post-1922 custody split:** County Antrim remained in the UK; pre-1922 records are held primarily at **PRONI** (Belfast), not the National Archives of Ireland in Dublin.
- **Denominations present:** Church of Ireland (rectory/vicarage), Presbyterian, Covenanters (Reformed Presbyterian), Wesleyan Methodists, Roman Catholic (part of the Coleraine RC district).

---

## Civil Registration

| Period | What exists |
|---|---|
| 1780–1844 | **Nothing** — no civil registration at all |
| 1845–1863 | Protestant marriages only |
| 1864–1870 | All births, deaths, and marriages |

**Gap:** The first 84 years of the target window are entirely undocumented by civil registration. Church records are the **sole primary source** for that span.

- **GRONI (General Register Office Northern Ireland):** Ferris House, Chichester Street, Belfast BT1 4HL — [nidirect.gov.uk/gro](https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/information-and-services/register-births-deaths-marriages-and-civil-partnerships/birth-death-and-marriage-certificates)

---

## Church Records

### Church of Ireland
- **Gap:** No digitized FamilySearch volume was found for Billy CoI registers. Whether they survived the **1922 Public Record Office fire** (which destroyed ~⅔ of pre-1870 CoI registers) is unconfirmed.
- **Check:** PRONI's free *Guide to Church Records* (download: [nidirect.gov.uk — Guide to Church Records, Oct 2019](https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/sites/default/files/publications/Guide-to-Church-Records-October-2019.pdf)) and the **RCB Library's List of Parish Registers**.
- **Gap-closing indexes:** Findmypast Ffolliott Collection — [baptisms](https://search.findmypast.com/search-world-Records/irish-parish-register-baptisms-and-confirmations-ffolliott-collection), [marriages](https://search.findmypast.com/search-world-records/irish-parish-register-marriages-ffolliott-collection), [burials](https://search.findmypast.com/search-world-records/irish-parish-register-burials-ffolliott-collection) (subscription).

### Presbyterian *(best online coverage)*
- **FamilySearch digitized volumes — Ballylinny/Billy:**
  - **Christenings 1837–1868** — 65 images, image group `007907410_008` — full-text searchable (not name-indexed)
  - **Marriages 1837–1864** — 50 images, image group `007765074_009` — full-text searchable
- **Gap — pre-1837:** No digitized Presbyterian volume before 1837. PRONI MIC 1P series holds microfilm.
- **Gap-closing indexes:** [RootsIreland.ie](http://www.rootsireland.ie/) (Ulster Historical Foundation); Findmypast — [Non-Conformist Baptisms](http://search.findmypast.com/search-world-Records/ireland-non-conformist-births-and-baptisms) and [Marriages](http://search.findmypast.com/search-world-records/ireland-non-conformist-marriages) (subscription).

### Covenanters (Reformed Presbyterian)
- **Gap:** No online index or digitized volume found for any date. Physical access at PRONI required.

### Wesleyan Methodists
- **Gap:** No online index or digitized volume found. Physical access at PRONI required.
- **Gap-closing index:** Findmypast — [Non-Conformist Congregational Records](http://search.findmypast.com/search-world-Records/ireland-non-conformist-congregational-records) (subscription).

### Roman Catholic
- **Gap — 1780–c.1828:** Virtually no Catholic registers expected (Catholic Emancipation 1828 is the practical floor).
- **Gap — c.1828–1870:** Billy falls in the **Coleraine RC district**; search Coleraine registers, not a Billy-specific series.
- **Gap-closing indexes:**
  - NLI Catholic Parish Registers portal (free): [registers.nli.ie](https://registers.nli.ie/)
  - Ancestry — Ireland, Catholic Parish Registers, 1655–1915, collection 61039: [ancestry.com](https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/61039/)
  - [RootsIreland.ie](http://www.rootsireland.ie/) (subscription)
  - Findmypast — [Ireland RC Parish Marriages](https://search.findmypast.com/search-world-records/ireland-roman-catholic-parish-marriages) (subscription)

---

## Census Substitutes (No Surviving Census for This Period)

Irish censuses 1821–1871 are almost entirely destroyed. Use:

| Record | Dates | FamilySearch volume |
|---|---|---|
| Tithe Applotment Books | 1823–1837 | Available on FamilySearch and Ancestry |
| Griffith's Primary Valuation | 1847–1864 | Ballylinny/Billy valuation 1867–1881: image group `004689599` (76 images, browse-only) |

---

## Other Key Record Types

- **Probate (post-1858):** PRONI. Pre-1858 indexes/abstracts: Findmypast — [Betham](https://search.findmypast.com/search-world-records/betham-genealogical-abstracts) and [Thrift Abstracts](https://search.findmypast.com/search-world-records/thrift-genealogical-abstracts) (compensate for 1922 fire losses).
- **Marriage License Bonds (pre-civil-reg):** FamilySearch collection 3460239 — Ireland, Diocesan and Prerogative Marriage License Bonds, 1623–1866 (Connor diocese covers County Antrim) — free.
- **School Records:** Deffrick National School Girls register, 1867–1933 — image group `008682995_005` (50 images, browse-only). Names children with father's name and residence.
- **Newspapers:** *Belfast Newsletter* (from 1737), *Coleraine Chronicle*, *Ballymena Observer* — marriage and death notices. Digitized runs at [britishnewspaperarchive.co.uk](https://www.britishnewspaperarchive.co.uk/) (subscription) and PRONI microfilm.
- **Military:** British Army records at The National Archives, Kew; militia/yeomanry records at PRONI.

---

## Repository Guide

### Online

| Repository | URL | Access | Key gap filled |
|---|---|---|---|
| FamilySearch | https://www.familysearch.org | Free | Presbyterian 1837–1868; school/valuation volumes |
| NLI Catholic Registers | https://registers.nli.ie/ | Free | Catholic registers (Coleraine district) |
| PRONI Digitised Church Records | https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/articles/digitised-church-records-available-proni | Free (some images) | Pre-1837 Presbyterian; CoI; Methodist; Covenanter |
| RootsIreland.ie | http://www.rootsireland.ie/ | Subscription | All Ulster denominations including pre-1837 |
| Ancestry | https://www.ancestry.com | Subscription | Catholic registers; Marriage License Bonds; Irish Records Index |
| Findmypast | https://www.findmypast.com | Subscription | Ffolliott (CoI); Non-Conformist; Betham/Thrift Abstracts |
| FamilySearch — Marriage License Bonds | https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/3460239 | Free | Pre-civil-registration marriages |

### Physical

| Repository | Address | What they hold |
|---|---|---|
| **PRONI** | 2 Titanic Boulevard, Titanic Quarter, Belfast BT3 9HQ · 028 9053 4800 · proni@communities-ni.gov.uk | All County Antrim church registers (original or microfilm); valuation; Tithe Applotment; estate papers; school registers; post-1858 wills; militia records |
| **RCB Library** | Braemor Park, Churchtown, Dublin 14, D14 N735 · +353 (0)1 492 3979 · library@ireland.anglican.org · [store.ireland.anglican.org/genealogy](https://store.ireland.anglican.org/genealogy) | Church of Ireland parish registers — surviving originals and finding aids |
| **National Archives of Ireland** | Bishop Street, Dublin D08 DF85 · mail@nationalarchives.ie · [nationalarchives.ie](http://www.nationalarchives.ie/) | Tithe Applotment originals; 1841/1851 census fragments; pre-1858 probate indexes |

---

## Known Record Losses

- **1922 PRO fire (Dublin):** Destroyed ~⅔ of pre-1870 Church of Ireland registers and most pre-1858 probate originals. Betham, Thrift, and Crossle abstracts (Findmypast) partially compensate.
- **1821–1871 census:** Almost entirely lost. Tithe Applotment and Griffith's Valuation are the only household substitutes.

---

## Research Tips

1. **Start with the PRONI Guide to Church Records** (free PDF linked above) — it lists every congregation in Billy parish, the register date ranges, and whether registers are at PRONI, the RCB Library, or the local church.
2. **The two FamilySearch Presbyterian volumes are full-text searchable, not name-indexed** — use FamilySearch's full-text search feature; then browse images to catch unusual spellings.
3. **Search CoI registers even for non-Anglican families** — baptisms, marriages, and burials of Dissenters were sometimes entered in CoI registers for legal purposes before 1845.
4. **For Catholic ancestors, search the Coleraine RC district**, not a Billy-specific series. Use NLI registers ([registers.nli.ie](https://registers.nli.ie/)) and Ancestry collection 61039.
5. **Use Tithe Applotment (1820s) + Griffith's (1847–1864) + the 1867–1881 Valuation scroll as a three-point household census** across the research window.
