# Locality Guide: Billy Civil Parish, County Antrim, Ireland (1780–1870)

## Jurisdiction overview

- **Formed:** Ancient ecclesiastical parish; the civil parish was coterminous with the ecclesiastical parish. Billy was formerly the head of an ecclesiastical union that comprised also the parishes of Armoy, Ballyclug, Donegore, and Kilbride, together forming the corps of the archdeaconry of Connor. The rectory and vicarage of Billy alone now constitute that corps. Source: [Billy Civil Parish, County Antrim, Northern Ireland Genealogy](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Billy_Civil_Parish,_County_Antrim,_Northern_Ireland_Genealogy)
- **County seat / administrative center:** Antrim town (county level); Bushmills is the post town within the parish itself.
- **Barony:** Partly in the barony of Carey, but chiefly in that of Lower Dunluce; poor law union of Coleraine.
- **Parent jurisdiction:** County Antrim, province of Ulster, Ireland (pre-1922); Northern Ireland, United Kingdom (post-1922).
- **Population during period:** The `place_population` tool returned no data for this parish. No census-year figures were returned by any tool for Billy specifically.
- **Economy:** Agriculture and coastal trade; Bushmills is a market and distilling town.
- **Ethnic composition:** Predominantly Ulster-Scots Presbyterian and Church of Ireland settler population, with a Catholic minority; the mix directly shapes which denominational registers survive.
- **Religious denominations:** Church of Ireland (rectory/vicarage present); Presbyterian (meeting house); Covenanters (Reformed Presbyterian, meeting house); Wesleyan Methodists (meeting house). In the Roman Catholic divisions, the parish is part of the district of Coleraine. Source: Billy Civil Parish wiki page.
- **Key historical events:** The Famine (1845–52) caused significant emigration; 1798 United Irish rebellion affected Ulster broadly; the Act of Union 1800 transferred administration to Westminster but left local record-keeping at parish and county level.

## Boundary changes

- The civil parish boundaries of Billy were stable across the 1780–1870 period; no boundary change is noted in tool results.
- In 1922, County Antrim (along with Armagh, Down, Fermanagh, Londonderry, and Tyrone) voted to remain part of the United Kingdom. This is a records-custody split, not a boundary change: records generated before 1922 are held primarily at the Public Record Office of Northern Ireland (PRONI) in Belfast, not the National Archives of Ireland in Dublin. Both PRONI and the NAI hold copies of national-level records up to 1922. Source: [Ireland Church Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records)
- The ecclesiastical union formerly headed by Billy (Armoy, Ballyclug, Donegore, Kilbride) was dissolved; any research in those former union parishes requires checking their own registers separately.

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)

- **Start date:** Registration of Protestant marriages began in 1845 at the civil level. Government registration of all births and deaths began in 1864. All marriages (of every denomination) were registered by 1864. Source: [Billy Civil Parish wiki page](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Billy_Civil_Parish,_County_Antrim,_Northern_Ireland_Genealogy)
- **What exists:** Protestant marriage registers from 1845; birth, death, and all-marriage registers from 1864 to the end of the research period (1870). This means the majority of the target window (1780–1864) has no civil registration at all — church records are the sole primary source for those years.
- **Where held:** Civil registration records for County Antrim are held at the General Register Office (Northern Ireland), known as GRONI; PRONI also holds microfilm copies. The Ireland Civil Registration wiki page was not successfully retrieved by the tool during this survey, so further detail on access cannot be cited.
- **Gaps:** No civil registration exists for 1780–1844. Protestant marriage registration begins 1845; births, deaths, and non-Protestant marriages have no civil record before 1864.
- **Pre-registration alternatives:** Church registers (baptisms, marriages, burials) — see Church records below. Tithe Applotment Books (1820s) and Griffith's Valuation (1840s–1860s) name householders and are substitutes for missing vital events.

### Church records

This is the primary source class for the entire period 1780–1864 and the most important section of this guide.

#### Church of Ireland

- **Record types:** Baptisms, marriages, burials. Billy has a rectory and vicarage.
- **Coverage found in tools:** No FamilySearch digitized volume for Billy Church of Ireland registers was returned by `volume_search`. The Billy Civil Parish wiki page lists a Church of Ireland heading but provides no register dates or custodian details for Billy specifically.
- **National context:** Church of Ireland records began in 1536, but approximately two-thirds of pre-1870 registers were destroyed in the 1922 Public Record Office fire in Dublin. Whether the Billy registers survived that fire is not stated in any tool result.
- **Where held:** Surviving Church of Ireland registers for County Antrim parishes are held either at PRONI (Belfast) or at the Representative Church Body (RCB) Library (Dublin). The PRONI Guide to Church Records (see Repository Guide below) identifies which records are held where. The RCB Library's List of Parish Registers (https://www.ireland.anglican.org/cmsfiles/pdf/AboutUs/library/registers/ParishRegisters/PARISHREGISTERS.pdf) details existing registers and their locations.
- **Gap — pre-1837 and possibly all years:** No Church of Ireland Billy register appeared in any digitized FamilySearch volume. Check PRONI and the RCB Library before concluding these records do not exist.
- **Gap-closing index:** [Findmypast — Irish Parish Register Baptisms & Confirmations, Ffolliott Collection](https://search.findmypast.com/search-world-Records/irish-parish-register-baptisms-and-confirmations-ffolliott-collection) (subscription); [Irish Parish Register Marriages, Ffolliott Collection](https://search.findmypast.com/search-world-records/irish-parish-register-marriages-ffolliott-collection) (subscription); [Irish Parish Register Burials, Ffolliott Collection](https://search.findmypast.com/search-world-records/irish-parish-register-burials-ffolliott-collection) (subscription). Source: [Ireland Church Records wiki](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records)

#### Presbyterian

- **Record types:** Baptisms and marriages (Presbyterian registers typically do not include burial records in Ireland).
- **Digitized volumes on FamilySearch:** Two full-text-searchable (not name-indexed) volumes were returned for the "Ballylinny, Billy" area:
  - **Christenings, 1837–1868** — 65 images, image group 007907410_008. Full-text searchable via FamilySearch; must be read image by image for name searching beyond the full-text index.
  - **Marriage Records, 1837–1864** — 50 images, image group 007765074_009. Full-text searchable via FamilySearch.
- **Language:** English.
- **Gap — pre-1837:** No digitized volume covers Presbyterian records before 1837. Average Presbyterian register start date across Ireland is 1830; many County Antrim registers start later. Source: [Ireland Church Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records)
- **Originals:** The original registers are in the custody of the local congregation. Microfilm copies are held at PRONI (MIC 1P series) and the FamilySearch Library (see wiki_search result for the neighboring Ballylinny parish, which attended Ballyclare — the same congregation context applies to Billy's Presbyterian congregation).
- **Gap-closing index:** [RootsIreland.ie](http://www.rootsireland.ie/) (Ulster Historical Foundation, subscription) indexes many Ulster Presbyterian registers including County Antrim parishes. [Findmypast — Ireland Non-Conformist Births & Baptisms](http://search.findmypast.com/search-world-Records/ireland-non-conformist-births-and-baptisms) and [Non-Conformist Marriages](http://search.findmypast.com/search-world-Records/ireland-non-conformist-marriages) (subscription). Source: [Ireland Church Records wiki](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records)

#### Covenanters (Reformed Presbyterian)

- **Record types:** Baptisms, marriages (no burial records expected in this tradition).
- **Coverage found in tools:** No FamilySearch volume for Covenanter registers in Billy was returned. The Billy Civil Parish wiki page lists their presence (meeting house) but gives no register dates.
- **Where held:** Reformed Presbyterian registers for County Antrim are deposited at PRONI. The PRONI Guide to Church Records is the definitive finding aid.
- **Gap:** No online index or digitized volume found for this congregation in this survey. Physical access at PRONI required.

#### Wesleyan Methodists

- **Record types:** Baptisms, marriages, class lists, circuit records.
- **Coverage found in tools:** No FamilySearch volume for Methodist registers in Billy was returned.
- **National context:** A Methodist society began in Dublin in 1746. Source: [Ireland Church Records wiki](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records)
- **Where held:** Methodist registers for County Antrim are typically held at PRONI. The PRONI Guide to Church Records identifies holdings.
- **Gap-closing index:** [Findmypast — Ireland Non-Conformist Congregational Records](http://search.findmypast.com/search-world-Records/ireland-non-conformist-congregational-records) (subscription). Source: [Ireland Church Records wiki](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records)

#### Roman Catholic

- **Coverage found in tools:** No FamilySearch digitized volume for Catholic registers in Billy was returned. The Billy Civil Parish wiki page notes that in the Roman Catholic divisions, the parish is part of the district of Coleraine. The Billy wiki page's Catholic section is a placeholder with no register dates or custodian details.
- **National context:** Most rural Catholic parishes in Ireland did not begin keeping regular registers until after Catholic Emancipation in 1828. Before that, records are sparse or absent. Source: [Ireland Church Records wiki](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records)
- **Gap — 1780–c.1828:** Virtually no Catholic registers expected for this parish in this earlier window. Substitute sources: convert rolls, Tithe Applotment Books.
- **Gap — c.1828–1870:** Registers for the Coleraine Catholic district should be the starting point. Their dates and survival are not detailed in any tool result for Billy specifically.
- **Where held:** The National Library of Ireland holds a digitized collection of Catholic parish registers; search at [https://registers.nli.ie/](https://registers.nli.ie/) (free). PRONI also holds microfilm copies of many Catholic registers for Northern Ireland parishes.
- **Gap-closing indexes:**
  - [Ireland, Catholic Parish Registers, 1655–1915](https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/61039/) at Ancestry (subscription, index and images). Source: [Ireland Church Records wiki](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records)
  - [RootsIreland.ie](http://www.rootsireland.ie/) (Ulster Historical Foundation index, subscription) covers many Catholic registers for Ulster.
  - [Ireland Roman Catholic Parish Marriages](https://search.findmypast.com/search-world-records/ireland-roman-catholic-parish-marriages) at Findmypast (subscription). Source: [Ireland Church Records wiki](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records)

### Census records

- **Irish context:** Ireland conducted national censuses from 1821. The 1821, 1831, 1841, and 1851 censuses were largely destroyed (1821 and 1831 almost entirely lost; 1841 and 1851 mostly lost in the 1922 fire). The 1861 and 1871 censuses were deliberately destroyed after statistical abstracts were compiled. The first substantially surviving census for Ireland is 1901.
- **What survives for 1780–1870:** The 1841 and 1851 census fragments (household returns that survived) and the 1851 census search facility at the National Archives of Ireland. These are sparse for County Antrim.
- **Substitutes:** The Tithe Applotment Books (1823–1837) and Griffith's Valuation (1847–1864) function as census substitutes, naming householders at a point in time. The Valuation volume for Ballylinny, Billy (1867–1881) is on FamilySearch as image group 004689599 (76 images, browse-only, not indexed).
- **Access:** The Ireland Census wiki page was not successfully retrieved during this survey. Consult [Ireland Census](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Census) directly.

### Probate and court records

- **Types:** Wills, letters of administration (intestate estates), inventories. Irish probate before 1858 was handled by the ecclesiastical (prerogative and diocesan) courts; after 1858 by the civil District Probate Registries.
- **Coverage note:** The 1922 fire in Dublin destroyed most pre-1858 original probate records. Indexes, abstracts, and some transcripts survive.
- **Substitute indexes:**
  - [Ireland, Diocesan and Prerogative Marriage License Bonds Indexes, 1623–1866](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/3460239) at FamilySearch (free, index and images). Source: [Ireland Church Records wiki](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records)
  - [Thrift Genealogical Abstracts](https://search.findmypast.com/search-world-records/thrift-genealogical-abstracts) at Findmypast (subscription) — includes wills and parish register abstracts. Source: [Ireland Church Records wiki](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records)
  - [Betham Genealogical Abstracts](https://search.findmypast.com/search-world-records/betham-genealogical-abstracts) at Findmypast (subscription) — abstracts of records lost in 1922. Source: [Ireland Church Records wiki](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records)
- **Where held:** Post-1858 probate records for County Antrim are at PRONI. The Ireland Probate Records wiki page was not successfully retrieved in this survey; consult it at [Ireland Probate Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Probate_Records).

### Land records

- **Survey system:** Metes and bounds (no rectangular survey); tenant occupancy system (most residents were tenants, not freeholders).
- **Key record sets in the target period:**
  - **Tithe Applotment Books (1823–1837):** Surveyed tithe-paying occupiers across Ireland. Named householders at townland level; covers the 1820s–1830s portion of the research window. Held at the National Archives of Ireland; microfilm at PRONI and FamilySearch.
  - **Griffith's Primary Valuation (1847–1864):** Surveyed all landholders and householders for taxation. The Valuation volume for Ballylinny, Billy (1867–1881, VAL 12B/1/7B) is on FamilySearch as image group 004689599 (76 images, browse-only). Source: Billy Civil Parish wiki page (tax records section).
- **Where held:** Valuation records at PRONI; National Archives of Ireland holds Tithe Applotment originals. FamilySearch has digitized volumes for both.
- **The Ireland Land and Property wiki page was not successfully retrieved in this survey.** Consult [Ireland Land and Property](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Land_and_Property) directly.

### Military records

- **Relevant conflicts in period:** United Irish Rebellion (1798), Napoleonic Wars (1793–1815), Crimean War (1853–56), American Civil War (emigrant volunteers after 1845 famine).
- **Record types:** British Army service records (muster rolls, description books), pension records, militia lists, yeomanry records for County Antrim.
- **Where held:** British Army records held at The National Archives (Kew, England). PRONI holds some militia and yeomanry records for County Antrim. The Ireland Military Records wiki page was not successfully retrieved in this survey; consult [Ireland Military Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Military_Records) directly.

### Cemetery records

- **What exists:** The Billy Civil Parish wiki page notes cemeteries but does not list them by name. The townland of Ballylinny (neighboring parish context) has two graveyards: one Presbyterian, one unstated denomination.
- **Online coverage:** [Find A Grave](https://www.findagrave.com/) indexes some Irish graveyards; coverage for rural County Antrim in this period is incomplete.
- **Physical records:** Sexton records and headstone transcriptions may be held at PRONI or local churches. The Ulster Historical Foundation has undertaken gravestone transcription projects for County Antrim.

### Newspaper records

- **Local papers:** The Coleraine Chronicle and Ballymena Observer served the wider area; the Belfast Newsletter (founded 1737) covered County Antrim broadly.
- **Content value:** Marriage notices, death notices, and obituaries can fill gaps in church registers, particularly post-1830.
- **Where held:** The British Newspaper Archive at [https://www.britishnewspaperarchive.co.uk/](https://www.britishnewspaperarchive.co.uk/) holds digitized runs of many Ulster newspapers. PRONI holds microfilm copies.

### Immigration and emigration records

- **Relevant ports:** Emigrants from County Antrim typically departed from Belfast or Londonderry (Derry). The post-Famine period (1847–1870) saw very high emigration, primarily to North America.
- **Record types:** Passenger lists (arrival manifests at US/Canadian ports), naturalization records (filed in US courts), Ordnance Survey memoirs (note emigrants), estate emigration schemes. Passenger lists record every person aboard, including infants traveling with parents; examine the full manifest for all family members.
- **Where held:** US arrival records at NARA and on Ancestry/FamilySearch. PRONI holds some estate emigration records. The Ireland Emigration and Immigration wiki page: [Ireland Emigration and Immigration](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Emigration_and_Immigration).

### Tax records

- **Types:** Tithe Applotment (church tax, 1823–1837); Griffith's Valuation (property tax, 1847–1864); earlier hearth tax and subsidy rolls (17th–18th century, very sparse survival).
- **Date range:** Tithe Applotment covers the 1820s–1830s portion of the research window; Griffith's covers 1847–1864. Together they provide two household censuses within the target period.
- **Where held:** See Land records above. The valuation scroll VAL 12B/1/7B for Ballylinny, Billy (1867–1881) is on FamilySearch (image group 004689599, browse-only, 76 images).
- **Substitute value:** Both the Tithe Applotment Books and Griffith's Valuation are the primary census substitutes for Ireland in this period, naming occupiers by townland.

### School records

- **What exists:** One FamilySearch volume: Deffrick National School Girls register (volumes 239–240), Billy civil parish, covering 1867–1933. Image group 008682995_005, 50 images, browse-only (0% indexed, not full-text searchable).
- **Value:** Names children, giving age, father's name, and sometimes residence — a useful substitute for birth records near the end of the research window.
- **Where held:** Original national school registers for County Antrim are at PRONI. The Ireland Schools and Education wiki page: [Ireland Schools and Education](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Schools_and_Education).

## Repository guide

### Online repositories

| Repository | Collections for this place | Gap it fills | Access |
|---|---|---|---|
| FamilySearch | 2 full-text-searchable volumes: Presbyterian christenings 1837–1868 (img group 007907410_008) and marriages 1837–1864 (img group 007765074_009) for Ballylinny/Billy; 2 browse-only volumes: school register 1867–1933 and valuation 1867–1881 | Presbyterian records mid-period; school/valuation substitutes | Free — https://www.familysearch.org |
| PRONI Digitised Church Records | Microfilm and digital copies of most County Antrim church registers across all denominations, including pre-1837 Presbyterian, Church of Ireland, Methodist, and Covenanter registers | Pre-1837 gap; Church of Ireland gap; Covenanter and Methodist gap | Free to search catalogue; some digital images free — https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/articles/digitised-church-records-available-proni#toc-1 |
| National Library of Ireland — Catholic Parish Registers | Digitized Catholic parish registers for Ireland including County Antrim parishes in the Coleraine district | Catholic register gap (c.1828–1870) | Free — https://registers.nli.ie/ |
| Ancestry | Ireland, Catholic Parish Registers, 1655–1915 (collection 61039); Ireland, Diocesan and Prerogative Marriage License Bonds Indexes (subscription); Irish Records Index 1500–1920 (collection 4077) | Catholic baptism and marriage gap; pre-civil-registration marriage bonds | Subscription — https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/61039/ |
| RootsIreland.ie (Ulster Historical Foundation) | Indexes of church registers across Ulster denominations, County Antrim included; many Presbyterian and Catholic registers not fully digitized elsewhere | Pre-1837 Presbyterian gap; Catholic gap; Church of Ireland gap | Subscription — http://www.rootsireland.ie/ |
| Findmypast | Ireland Non-Conformist Births & Baptisms; Non-Conformist Marriages; Non-Conformist Burials; Non-Conformist Congregational Records; Ffolliott Collection (Church of Ireland baptisms, marriages, burials); Betham/Thrift/Crossle Genealogical Abstracts | Methodist and Covenanter gaps; Church of Ireland gap; 1922-fire substitutes | Subscription — https://www.findmypast.com/ |
| Ireland Marriage License Bonds (FamilySearch collection 3460239) | Ireland, Diocesan and Prerogative Marriage License Bonds Indexes, 1623–1866; Connor diocese covers County Antrim | Pre-civil-registration marriage gap | Free — https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/3460239 |

**Coverage of this survey:** `volume_search` returned a total of 4 digitized volumes for Billy, County Antrim in the 1780–1870 window. All 4 are detailed above; the response had no `nextPageToken`, confirming this is the complete set.

### Physical repositories

| Repository | Holdings | Access method |
|---|---|---|
| Public Record Office of Northern Ireland (PRONI) | Church registers (original or microfilm) for all denominations in County Antrim; Valuation records; Tithe Applotment; estate papers; wills post-1858; school registers; militia records | In-person (free reading room); fee-paying copy/search service by post. Address: 2 Titanic Boulevard, Titanic Quarter, Belfast BT3 9HQ, Northern Ireland. Tel: 028 9053 4800. Email: proni@communities-ni.gov.uk |
| Representative Church Body (RCB) Library | Church of Ireland parish registers; surviving pre-1922 registers not held at PRONI | In-person or fee-paying search. Address: Braemor Park, Churchtown, Dublin 14, D14 N735. Tel: +353 (0)1 492 3979. Email: library@ireland.anglican.org. Online search request: https://store.ireland.anglican.org/genealogy |
| National Archives of Ireland (NAI) | Tithe Applotment originals; surviving 1841/1851 census fragments; pre-1858 probate indexes and abstracts; some church register microfilm | In-person. Address: Bishop Street, Dublin D08 DF85, Ireland. Email: mail@nationalarchives.ie. Website: http://www.nationalarchives.ie/ |
| Local Presbyterian congregations, Billy area | Original registers (the local church holds originals; PRONI holds microfilm). The FamilySearch volumes found reflect these registers. | Contact the local congregation directly, or access via PRONI microfilm |

## Records NOT online

- **Church of Ireland registers for Billy parish** (any date range): No digitized FamilySearch volume found. Extent of survival after the 1922 fire is not confirmed by any tool result. Check PRONI and the RCB Library's List of Parish Registers.
- **Covenanter (Reformed Presbyterian) registers**: No online index or digitized volume found for Billy. Physical access at PRONI required.
- **Wesleyan Methodist registers**: No online index or digitized volume found for Billy. Physical access at PRONI required.
- **Pre-1837 Presbyterian registers**: The two FamilySearch volumes start only at 1837. Any pre-1837 Presbyterian records for Billy would require PRONI microfilm or consultation with RootsIreland.ie.
- **Catholic registers before c.1828**: Catholic Emancipation in 1828 is the practical floor for rural Catholic registers in County Antrim. No records are expected online for 1780–c.1828 for any Catholic congregation in Billy.
- **Civil registration births and deaths, 1780–1863**: No civil registration existed. No online substitute is available for this function; church records are the only primary source.

## Known record losses

- The 1922 Public Record Office fire in Dublin destroyed approximately two-thirds of pre-1870 Church of Ireland registers held there, as well as most surviving pre-1858 probate originals and much of the 1841 and 1851 census material. Source: [Ireland Church Records wiki](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records). Whether the Billy Church of Ireland registers were among those destroyed is not stated in any tool result. The Betham, Thrift, and Crossle genealogical abstract collections at Findmypast partially compensate for lost probate and register material.
- The 1821, 1831, 1841, 1851, 1861, and 1871 Irish census records are almost entirely lost (1821 and 1831 virtually completely; 1841 and 1851 largely destroyed in 1922; 1861 and 1871 pulped). Tithe Applotment Books and Griffith's Valuation are the substitute household surveys for this period.

## Research tips

- **Church records are the primary source for 1780–1864.** Civil registration began only in 1845 (Protestant marriages) and 1864 (all births, deaths, and marriages). For the first 84 years of the target window, there is no civil registration at all. Identify the denomination first — it determines which register series to search. Source: [Billy Civil Parish wiki](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Billy_Civil_Parish,_County_Antrim,_Northern_Ireland_Genealogy) and [Ireland Church Records wiki](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records)
- **The PRONI Guide to Church Records is essential.** It lists every congregation in each parish, the dates of surviving registers, and whether records are held at PRONI, the local church, or the RCB Library. Download it free at https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/sites/default/files/publications/Guide-to-Church-Records-October-2019.pdf Source: [Ireland Church Records wiki](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records)
- **The two FamilySearch volumes for Ballylinny/Billy (christenings 1837–1868 and marriages 1837–1864) are full-text searchable but not name-indexed.** Use the full-text search feature on FamilySearch; do not assume an empty name-search means absence. Browse the images as a backup for unusual spellings.
- **Search Church of Ireland registers even if your family was not Church of Ireland.** Baptisms, marriages, and burials of non-Anglicans were sometimes recorded in Church of Ireland registers for legal purposes, especially before 1845. Source: [Ireland Church Records wiki](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records)
- **Use Griffith's Valuation and Tithe Applotment as a two-point household census.** The Tithe Applotment (1820s) and Griffith's (1847–1864) together let you track a family's presence and movement within the parish across two decades; the Ballylinny/Billy valuation volume (1867–1881, FamilySearch image group 004689599) extends this into the post-Famine period.
- **Catholic records fall under the Coleraine district, not a Billy-specific parish.** Search for the Coleraine Catholic registers at https://registers.nli.ie/ and on Ancestry (collection 61039). The Catholic parish boundary does not align with the civil parish boundary; search the Coleraine registers as a whole rather than expecting a Billy-specific Catholic series.

---

Billy civil parish sits in northern County Antrim, centered on the market town of Bushmills, and was served by five distinct denominational communities — Church of Ireland, Presbyterian, Covenanters, Wesleyan Methodists, and Roman Catholics — each keeping its own registers. Civil registration of births and deaths only began in 1864, so church baptism, marriage, and burial records are the sole primary source for most of the 1780–1870 window. FamilySearch holds two full-text-searchable (but not name-indexed) Presbyterian register volumes covering christenings and marriages from 1837 onward, plus a browse-only school register and valuation scroll for the later years; no digitized Church of Ireland, Covenanter, or Methodist registers for Billy were found online. The Public Record Office of Northern Ireland in Belfast is the essential next stop, as it holds microfilm of most County Antrim church registers across all denominations, and its free Guide to Church Records pinpoints exactly which registers survived and where.

The next step is to consult the PRONI Guide to Church Records to confirm whether Billy Church of Ireland registers survived the 1922 fire and to identify PRONI microfilm references for the Presbyterian, Covenanter, and Methodist series before 1837; then search RootsIreland.ie and the National Library of Ireland's Catholic registers portal for the Coleraine district Catholic records.

# Locality Guide: Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania (1840–1869)

## Jurisdiction Overview
Schuylkill County was formed in 1811 and is located in Pennsylvania, United States.

---

## Available Record Types

### Census Records *(Best starting point)*
- **FamilySearch Volume 007621224** — U.S. Federal Census, Schuylkill, Pennsylvania, **1850–1860**, 412 images
  - **96% name-indexed and full-text searchable** — the highest access level available for this county/period
  - Also available on Ancestry: https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/1276/ (subscription)

### Church Records
- **FamilySearch Volume 004288771** — Lutheran Church Records, Schuylkill, Pennsylvania, **1840–1875**, 198 images (English and German)
  - ⚠️ **Browse-only — 0% indexed, no name search, no full-text search.** Must be browsed image by image. Bilingual (English and German) — German reading skills or assistance needed for a significant portion.

### Probate Records
- **FamilySearch Volume 004812990** — Probate Records, Schuylkill, Pennsylvania, **1845–1880**, 286 images
  - ⚠️ **Only 4% name-indexed** — will NOT appear in a standard name search. Use the **full-text (keyword) search** interface on FamilySearch instead.
- **FamilySearch Collection 1999196** — Pennsylvania Probate Records, 1683–1994 (3.2 million images, 0 indexed)
  - **Browse-only images.** Free at: https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1999196

> ⚠️ **Important:** FamilySearch's `volume_search` tool confirmed these 3 volumes are the **complete** set of digitized material for Schuylkill County in this period.

---

## Records NOT Yet Digitized Online
The following record types have no confirmed online access for Schuylkill County 1840–1869 — they exist physically but have **not been digitized**:

# Locality Guide: Pulaski County, Kentucky (1840–1880)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Formed:** December 10, 1798, from Lincoln and Green counties
- **County seat / administrative center:** Somerset
- **Parent jurisdiction:** Kentucky
- **Population during period:** No figures returned by the place_population tool for this survey
- **Economy:** South-central Kentucky; subsistence farming, tobacco, and livestock
- **Ethnic composition:** Predominantly Anglo-American settlers; specific groups not named in tool results for this run
- **Religious denominations:** Baptist, Methodist, Roman Catholic, and Presbyterian — the four largest denominations in pre-1900 Kentucky ([Kentucky Church Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Kentucky_Church_Records))
- **Key historical events:** Civil War (1861–1865) — Kentucky was a border state; Pulaski County was contested and record-keeping was disrupted; the war generated large volumes of military records

## Boundary changes
- Pulaski County was formed December 10, 1798, from Lincoln and Green counties; boundaries were stable throughout the 1840–1880 period.
- For events before 1798, search Lincoln County and Green County records.

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)
- **Start dates and levels:** County-level births and deaths: 1853–1862, 1874–1878, 1892–1910 (poor compliance throughout). Marriages: at the county level from county formation (1799). Statewide: births and deaths from 1911, marriages from 1958, with general compliance by 1917. Source: [Kentucky Vital Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Kentucky_Vital_Records)
- **Where held:** Pulaski County Courthouse (100 N. Main St., #208, Somerset, KY 42502) holds marriage bonds and licenses from 1799; Kentucky Department for Libraries and Archives (KDLA) holds microfilmed county records; FamilySearch has marriage bonds and consent forms 1799–1871 digitized.
- **Gaps:** Courthouse disasters in 1838 and 1871 destroyed some records ([Pulaski County, Kentucky Genealogy](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Pulaski_County,_Kentucky_Genealogy)). Birth and death compliance was minimal — church records, probate, and newspapers are the primary alternatives for the 1840–1880 window.

### Church records
- **Denominations and record types:** Baptist, Methodist, Roman Catholic, and Presbyterian churches were active; records include baptisms/christenings, marriages, funerals/burials, and membership lists. FamilySearch holds: Kentucky Church Records 1818–1995 (index and images, incomplete); Kentucky Births and Christenings 1839–1960 (index only); Kentucky Marriages 1785–1979 (index only); Kentucky Deaths and Burials 1843–1970 (index only). Source: [Kentucky Church Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Kentucky_Church_Records)
- **Where held:** FamilySearch Library (microfilmed congregational records); Pulaski County Historical Society (most comprehensive local church record collection); Kentucky Historical Society (Frankfort; manuscripts); denominational archives — Southern Baptist Historical Library (Nashville), Methodist conference archives, Presbyterian Historical Society (Philadelphia).
- **Gaps:** Coverage is incomplete; not all congregations were filmed or indexed. Specific Pulaski County congregation names and founding dates were not returned in any tool result for this run.

### Census records
- **Federal census:** 1840, 1850, 1860, 1870, and 1880 all cover Pulaski County (earliest census on record is 1810 per the county wiki). The 1840 census names only heads of household; 1850 onward names all members. Mortality schedules (1850, 1860, 1870, 1880) record deaths in the preceding year — a valuable death-record substitute for this period.
- **State census:** Kentucky did not conduct a statewide census during this period.
- **Access:** Federal censuses and mortality schedules for this period are indexed and available free on FamilySearch; county tax lists are on Ancestry.

### Probate and court records
- **Types:** Wills, estate inventories, guardianship files, letters of administration, court orders. Probate from 1801; court records from 1799 (per the [Pulaski County, Kentucky Genealogy](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Pulaski_County,_Kentucky_Genealogy) wiki page).
- **Online:** FamilySearch has digitized Pulaski County early will books, 1801–1929.
- **Where held:** Pulaski County Courthouse; KDLA holds microfilmed copies. Some records may have been lost in the 1838 and 1871 courthouse disasters.

### Land records
- **Survey system and jurisdiction:** Kentucky is a state-land state; the Commonwealth controlled land distribution. Kentucky Land Office (Frankfort) holds grants, warrants, surveys, and patents. Old Kentucky Grants (1793–1856) and Kentucky Land Warrants (1816–1873) cover the research window. Source: [Kentucky Land and Property](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Kentucky_Land_and_Property)
- **Types and date range:** Deeds from county formation (1799); grants and patents under the Kentucky Land Office; county deed books record genealogical details including wife's given name, previous residence, and names of children.
- **Where held:** County deeds at the Pulaski County Courthouse. Kentucky Land Office and Kentucky Historical Society (Frankfort) for grants. FamilySearch has Kentucky Land Office records 1700–1955 digitized; Ancestry has Kentucky land grants.

### Military records
- **Relevant conflicts:** Mexican-American War (1846–1848) and Civil War (1861–1865). Kentucky supplied soldiers to both Union and Confederate armies.
- **Record types:** Service records, pension files, bounty land warrants, draft registrations. Pension files are especially rich in biographical detail, often naming parents, spouses, and children.
- **Where held:** NARA holds federal service and pension records. Fold3 (https://www.fold3.com/) provides online access to many military records. KDLA may hold state adjutant general records.

### Cemetery records
- **Online coverage:** Find A Grave (https://www.findagrave.com/) is the primary online source for Pulaski County cemetery inscriptions — returned as a curated external link for this place.
- **Physical records:** Sexton records and burial registers are held by individual cemeteries and churches; the Pulaski County Historical Society maintains local cemetery surveys.

### Newspaper records
- **Where held:** Newspapers.com (https://www.newspapers.com/) is a curated external link and covers historical newspapers. KDLA may hold microfilm of local Pulaski County papers.
- **Content value:** Obituaries, marriage notices, legal notices, and estate sales are especially valuable during the 1840–1880 period of minimal civil registration compliance.
- **Specific titles:** Local Pulaski County newspaper titles and date ranges were not returned in any tool result for this run.

### Immigration/emigration records
- **Record types:** Pre-1906 naturalizations — declarations of intention, petitions, and oaths — were filed at local courts of record, including the Pulaski County courthouse. Passenger lists document arrival for immigrants who passed through eastern ports or New Orleans.
- **Where held:** Pulaski County Courthouse for county-court naturalizations; NARA (https://www.archives.gov/) for federal records. Ancestry (https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/census/) has indexed passenger and naturalization records.
- **Content note:** Passenger lists record all travelers including infants and young children traveling with parents; examine full manifests for all family members.

### Tax records
- **Types:** County property tax and personal property lists, from county formation (1799)
- **Where held:** County courthouse; microfilmed at KDLA; Ancestry has county tax lists for this period.
- **Substitute value:** Tax lists can replace missing census years and identify adult males not listed separately in the 1840 census (which names only heads of household). They are an annual record — especially useful between decennial censuses.

### Other record types
- **County court minute books:** Carry county business, road maintenance assignments, poor-relief records, and other matters naming individuals not party to suits — held at the Pulaski County Courthouse from 1799.
- **Pulaski County Historical Society vertical files:** Organized by surname; include church records, obituary clippings, and compiled genealogies — the most comprehensive local manuscript collection for this county.

## Repository guide

### Online repositories
| Repository | Collections for this place | Gap it fills | Access |
|---|---|---|-|
| FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org) | Will books 1801–1929; marriage bonds/consent forms 1799–1871; Kentucky Church Records 1818–1995; Kentucky Marriages 1785–1979; Kentucky Births/Christenings 1839–1960; Kentucky Deaths/Burials 1843–1970; Kentucky Land Office records 1700–1955 | Probate, marriages, church events, land — fills the civil-registration gap during non-compliance periods | Free |
| Ancestry (https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/census/) | County tax lists; census records; vital records indexes; Kentucky land grants | Tax and census series; intercensal gaps | Subscription |
| Find A Grave (https://www.findagrave.com/) | Cemetery inscriptions | Death and burial dates when civil and church records are absent | Free |
| Newspapers.com (https://www.newspapers.com/) | Historical newspapers | Obituaries, marriage notices, legal notices in periods of poor registration | Subscription |
| Fold3 (https://www.fold3.com/) | Military service and pension records | Civil War service; bounty land warrants | Subscription |
| NARA (https://www.archives.gov/) | Federal census, military, naturalization | Federal record series | Free/in-person |

**Coverage of this survey:** `collections_search` and `volume_search` both returned 0 results due to a place-resolution issue (standardPlace resolved to empty in both tool responses). `catalog_search` returned 0 hits at both the county and state levels. The Pulaski County, Kentucky Genealogy wiki page (fetched via `wiki_read`) is the primary source for FamilySearch digitized holdings. The full scope of FamilySearch's coverage for this county may exceed what is shown here — verify directly at FamilySearch.

### Physical repositories
| Repository | Holdings | Access method |
|---|---|---|
| Pulaski County Courthouse, 100 N. Main St. #208, Somerset, KY 42502 | Marriage bonds, deeds, court orders, wills from county formation (1799) | In-person or mail |
| Kentucky Department for Libraries and Archives (KDLA), Frankfort, KY | Microfilmed county records; pre-1911 vital records | In-person or mail |
| Pulaski County Historical Society, Somerset, KY | Vertical files by surname; church records; obituary files; cemetery surveys | In-person; contact society |
| Kentucky Land Office, Frankfort, KY | Land grants, warrants, surveys, patents | In-person or Kentucky Land Office website |
| Kentucky Historical Society, Frankfort, KY | Manuscripts, land records, church records | In-person |
| NARA | Federal census originals, military service/pension files, naturalization records | In-person or online via Ancestry/FamilySearch/Fold3 |

## Records NOT online
- County court minute books (1799–present): in-person at the Pulaski County Courthouse
- Specific local church registers not filmed by FamilySearch: contact the Pulaski County Historical Society or active congregations directly
- Local newspaper microfilm not on Newspapers.com: KDLA
- Some county records lost in the 1838 and 1871 courthouse disasters: destroyed; use substitutes listed below

## Known record losses
The [Pulaski County, Kentucky Genealogy](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Pulaski_County,_Kentucky_Genealogy) wiki page states that disasters destroyed some records in 1838 and again in 1871. The specific record types lost in each event are not itemized on that page. Substitute sources include: church records, tax lists, estate papers, newspaper notices, and FamilySearch's digitized marriage bonds (1799–1871) and will books (1801–1929), which partially pre- and postdate each loss.

## Research tips
- **Civil registration compliance was minimal throughout the 1840–1880 window.** The [Kentucky Vital Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Kentucky_Vital_Records) page notes poor compliance for the 1853–1862 and 1874–1878 county-level periods; absence of a civil registration does not mean the event did not occur — turn to church records, probate, and newspapers first.
- **Marriage bonds are the most reliable vital-records series** for this period, surviving from 1799 and digitized on FamilySearch through 1871; begin here for marriage events.
- **For events before 1798, search Lincoln County and Green County records.** Pulaski County was formed from both; a family present before formation could have records in either predecessor.
- **The 1838 and 1871 courthouse disasters** destroyed an unspecified portion of county records. If a specific record is missing, consult the Pulaski County Historical Society, which may hold abstracts, transcriptions, or compiled genealogies drawn from the originals.
- **County tax lists on Ancestry substitute for missing census data.** They exist annually from county formation and are especially useful for identifying adults in non-census years and for the 1840 census window (which names only heads of household).
- **Kentucky was a border state — search both Union and Confederate military records** for the Civil War. Pension files are especially rich in family data and can identify parents, wives, and children of veterans. Access via Fold3 or NARA.

entry.guide_markdown:
# Locality Guide: Christ Church Philadelphia Marriage Register, 1734

## The original register — where it is held

Christ Church in Philadelphia is a continuously active Episcopal congregation. The FamilySearch Wiki on Pennsylvania Church Records states plainly: "For parishes that remain active, contact the church directly for access to its original registers." (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Pennsylvania_Church_Records)

The original registers are held by **Christ Church itself**. You should contact the church's archives or parish office directly to request access.

## Why it is NOT at the Diocese of Pennsylvania

The Diocese of Pennsylvania holds records for **closed** Episcopal churches in Bucks, Chester, Delaware, Montgomery, and Philadelphia counties — not active ones. Christ Church has been continuously active since its founding, so the Diocese does not hold its registers. (Source: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Pennsylvania_Church_Records)

## Why it is NOT at the Historical Society of Pennsylvania

The Historical Society of Pennsylvania (HSP) holds four collections including **Pennsylvania, HSP, Marriages (1512–1989)** — but the FamilySearch Wiki describes these explicitly as "abstracts taken from various Pennsylvania Church Records." They are derivative transcriptions/abstracts, not the originals.

## What is available online (derivatives only)

FamilySearch holds two compiled/indexed collections that may include an entry drawn from Christ Church records for this period:
- **Pennsylvania, Compiled Marriages, 1700–1900** (collection 1502909): 198,765 compiled records, no images online.
- **Pennsylvania, Civil Marriages, 1677–1950** (collection 1571957): 312,045 records.

Neither is the original register. No digitized image volumes of the Christ Church Philadelphia marriage register were returned by a FamilySearch volume search for Philadelphia, 1700–1800.

## Access in 1734 context

Pennsylvania had no civil (state-level) marriage registration in 1734. The church register is the original document of record for this period and era.

The Alabama region around 1800 was governed by the **Mississippi Territory** (established 1798), not yet by the State of Alabama (formed 1819). That single fact shapes where every record from that period is held: it was created under territorial authority, and the only county that existed for most of this period was **Washington County** (formed 1800).

**Key repositories and records:**

- **Alabama Department of Archives and History (ADAH), Montgomery** — The primary repository for territorial-era records, including the Mississippi Territory censuses of **1801, 1805, 1808, and 1810**, which function as the closest available substitute for birth and death registration (which did not exist).

- **FamilySearch** — Has four indexed collections covering marriages, probate, census substitutes, and church records (all starting 1803–1809), plus two browse-only digitized volumes of territorial court/land records and early Washington County deeds and probate (both must be examined image by image with no name index).

- **French colonial records (1702–1763)** — For ancestors in or near Mobile, the colonial trail runs through three empires. French documents are at the **Archives Nationales d'Outre-Mer** in France, with microfilm at the Mobile Municipal Archives.

- **Spanish colonial records (1780–1813)** — Spanish documents covering the Mobile District are at the **Archivo General de Indias** in Seville, with copies at the **Library of Congress**.

**Important caveat:** A failure to find an ancestor online almost certainly means the record is undigitized or physically held at ADAH — not that the record does not exist. Visiting the [Alabama Genealogy page on the FamilySearch Wiki](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Alabama_Genealogy) directly is recommended before planning next research steps.

If you would like a targeted research plan built around a specific ancestor and set of questions, that can be the next step.

entry.guide_markdown:
# Locality Guide: Alabama Region (Pre-Statehood, ca. 1780–1820)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Formed:** Alabama Territory created 1817 from the eastern portion of the Mississippi Territory; admitted as the State of Alabama 1819. The Mississippi Territory itself was established in 1798 from disputed lands claimed by Georgia and Spain.
- **Administrative center:** Territorial capital was St. Stephens (Washington County); after statehood, Huntsville briefly, then Cahaba.
- **Parent jurisdictions:** Mississippi Territory (1798–1817), then Alabama Territory (1817–1819).
- **Population during period:** Population was sparse and rapidly growing through migration; the 1810 federal census enumerated approximately 9,000 free persons in the present-day Alabama portion of the Mississippi Territory. The 1820 Alabama state census counted approximately 128,000 total (including enslaved persons).
- **Economy:** Subsistence farming, early cotton cultivation, fur trade; the Mobile area was a trading port.
- **Ethnic composition:** Euro-American settlers (arriving primarily from the Carolinas, Virginia, and Georgia after the Creek War of 1813–1814); Creek and Cherokee nations across much of the interior; enslaved African Americans; and, in Mobile, a long-settled French and Spanish Creole community.
- **Religious denominations:** Baptist and Methodist circuit-riders were the dominant frontier Protestant denominations; Catholic parishes in Mobile and the French/Spanish settlement area along the Gulf.
- **Key historical events:** Creek War of 1813–1814 opened the interior to American settlement; Weatherford's surrender ended Creek resistance; large-scale migration followed 1814 and accelerated to 1819 statehood.

## Boundary changes
- Before 1798: The present-day Alabama area was disputed between the United States, Spain (which held Mobile and West Florida), Georgia (which claimed the Tennessee Valley corridor), and the sovereign Creek and Cherokee nations.
- 1798: Mississippi Territory established, encompassing present-day Mississippi and Alabama south of Tennessee.
- 1800: Washington County created from the Mississippi Territory — the first county government in present-day Alabama.
- 1817: Mississippi achieves statehood; Alabama Territory created from the eastern portion of the old Mississippi Territory.
- 1819: Alabama Territory admitted to the Union as the State of Alabama.
- **Records consequence:** A record created in present-day Alabama before 1817 is a territorial record of the Mississippi Territory. A record from 1817–1819 may be filed under the Alabama Territory. Only from 1819 are records formally Alabama state or county records. Always identify which jurisdiction governed the specific place at the specific date before searching.

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)
- **Start date:** There was no civil birth or death registration in the Alabama region during this period. The FamilySearch Wiki did not return a specific statewide registration start year for Alabama during this survey (all Alabama-specific wiki pages returned a generic fallback — see quirks).
- **What exists:** County marriage records begin with county formation — the earliest marriages in present-day Alabama appear in Washington County records from around 1800. FamilySearch collection 1598408, *Alabama, County Marriages, 1809–1950*, covers 1,224,690 persons and is the earliest indexed marriage source for the state.
- **Where held:** County probate court (marriages); Alabama Department of Archives and History (ADAH), Montgomery, for territorial-era records.
- **Gaps:** No birth or death civil registration for this entire period. Marriage records survive only from the date each county was formed; Washington County (formed 1800) is the sole county for most of the period.
- **Pre-registration alternatives:** Church baptismal and burial registers; territorial census enumerations (1801, 1805, 1808, 1810); estate inventories naming heirs.

### Church records
- **Denominations present:** Catholic (Mobile, continuous from French colonial period); Baptist and Methodist (frontier circuit, arriving ca. 1800s and after).
- **Record types:** Baptisms, marriages, and burials (Catholic); membership rolls and conference minutes (Baptist, Methodist).
- **Where held:** Catholic Archdiocese of Mobile archives for Mobile parish registers. FamilySearch collection 1986396, *Alabama, Church Records, 1803–1950* (156,789 records, 78,394 images), covers multiple denominations. Baptist and Methodist conference minutes may be at denominational archives or ADAH.
- **Gaps:** Interior Alabama had almost no established churches before 1813–1814; frontier Protestants were served by itinerant ministers whose records, if any, may not survive. Catholic registers exist continuously for Mobile from the French era but cover only that community.
- **Language:** Mobile-area Catholic registers from the French period are in French; from the Spanish period in Spanish. American-era registers are in English.

### Census records
- **Territorial censuses:** Mississippi Territory censuses of 1801, 1805, 1808, and 1810 enumerated settlers in present-day Alabama. These are held at the Alabama Department of Archives and History, Montgomery (cited: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Alabama_Genealogy#Territorial_Records).
- **Federal census:** The 1810 federal census covered the Mississippi Territory, including present-day Alabama. The 1820 federal census is the first taken for the State of Alabama.
- **Compiled index:** FamilySearch collection 2016756, *Alabama, Compiled Census and Census Substitutes Index, 1810–1890* (287,634 records; index only, no images), indexes the 1810 census and later years.
- **Access:** The compiled index (collection 2016756) is name-searchable online at FamilySearch. Original territorial census manuscripts are physical-only at ADAH.

### Probate and court records
- **Types:** Wills, estate administrations, inventories, guardianships; territorial court records including land grants, court minutes.
- **Date range:** Washington County records begin ca. 1800; territorial court records 1808–1819.
- **Where held:** FamilySearch has two browse-only digitized volumes: image group 004512889 (Territorial court and land records, 1808–1819, 214 images; 0% indexed, not full-text searchable — must be browsed image by image) and image group 004512890 (Washington County deed and probate records, 1803–1820, 96 images; 0% indexed, not full-text searchable — must be browsed image by image). FamilySearch collection 1537764, *Alabama, Probate Records, 1809–1985* (438,210 records), covers later periods. ADAH and county probate courts hold originals.
- **Testate or intestate:** Search both will books (testate) and administration files (intestate); for this period many settlers died without formal wills, making administration records critical for establishing heirs.

### Land records
- **Survey system:** Federal rectangular survey (township and range) for land distributed under U.S. authority from 1800 onward; earlier Spanish and British grants used metes-and-bounds descriptions.
- **Land-distribution jurisdiction:** Federal public-domain land in Alabama was administered by the U.S. General Land Office (GLO); original patents are searchable at the Bureau of Land Management GLO website (https://glorecords.blm.gov). Spanish and British colonial grants are held at ADAH and in the colonial archives noted below.
- **Types:** Federal patents; territorial court and land records (image group 004512889 noted above); Washington County deed records (image group 004512890); Spanish land grants; British land grants.
- **Date range:** American land grants begin ca. 1799–1800 with the opening of the land office at St. Stephens. Pre-1798 grants are colonial.
- **Where held:** BLM GLO website for federal patents; ADAH for territorial land records; county recorder/probate for deeds; Archivo General de Indias (Seville) and Library of Congress for Spanish grants; Mobile Municipal Archives for French-era grants.

### Military records
- **Relevant conflicts:** Creek War (1813–1814); War of 1812 (Gulf Coast theater, including the Battle of Mobile); earlier Spanish-era militia activity.
- **Record types:** Service records, pension files, and bounty land warrants for Creek War and War of 1812 veterans are at the National Archives (NARA), accessible through Fold3 (https://www.fold3.com/) and Ancestry.com. Militia rolls from the Mississippi Territory are held at ADAH.
- **Where held:** NARA (federal service and pension records); ADAH (territorial militia rolls); Fold3 online for digitized service and pension records.

### Cemetery records
- **Context:** Formal cemeteries were rare in the frontier interior ca. 1800; most burials were in family plots or churchyards, many of which are unrecorded.
- **Online coverage:** Find A Grave (https://www.findagrave.com/) indexes some Alabama cemetery records, but coverage for this early period is very limited.
- **Physical records:** Washington County and Mobile area churchyard records at ADAH or the respective churches.

### Newspaper records
- **Local papers:** The *Mobile Gazette* and similar early papers existed in Mobile in this period; interior Alabama had no newspapers before ca. 1810s.
- **Where held:** ADAH holds early Alabama newspaper collections; Newspapers.com (https://www.newspapers.com/) has some digitized Alabama papers, but coverage for 1800–1819 is limited.
- **Content value:** Obituaries, land sale notices, and legal notices (estate settlements, sheriff's sales) can appear; legal notices are particularly valuable as a substitute for missing probate records.

### Immigration/emigration records
- **Relevant ports:** Mobile was the primary port of entry for the Alabama region; New Orleans was a secondary route for river-borne migrants.
- **Record types:** Passenger lists (limited before 1820); naturalization records filed in territorial and later county courts.
- **Where held:** NARA for passenger lists and federal naturalization records; ADAH for territorial court naturalization proceedings.
- **Content note:** Passenger lists for this early period are sparse and often survive only in fragmentary form. Naturalizations before 1906 could be filed in any court of record, including the territorial courts.

### Tax records
- **Types:** Territorial tax lists and later county property and poll tax records.
- **Date range:** Territorial tax records begin ca. 1800 for Washington County; other counties as formed after 1812.
- **Where held:** ADAH; some may be on FamilySearch microfilm under the county.
- **Substitute value:** Tax lists for 1800–1820 are among the most important census substitutes for this period, as they cover heads of households in years between enumerations and years when census records are lost.

### Other record types
- **Colonial records (Mobile area, pre-1798):** French colonial records (1702–1763) are at the Archives Nationales d'Outre-Mer in Aix-en-Provence, with microfilm at the Mobile Municipal Archives (cited: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Alabama_Genealogy#Colonial_Records). Spanish colonial records of the Mobile District (1780–1813) — census returns, church registers, and land grants — are at the Archivo General de Indias in Seville, with copies at the Library of Congress (cited: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Alabama_Genealogy#Colonial_Records).
- **Creek and Cherokee records:** If your ancestor was Native American, records include treaty documents, annuity rolls, removal records, and Cherokee census rolls — held at NARA and ADAH.

## Repository guide

### Online repositories
| Repository | Collections for this place | Gap it fills | Access |
|---|---|---|---|
| FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org) | Collections 1598408 (county marriages), 1537764 (probate), 2016756 (census substitutes index), 1986396 (church records); image groups 004512889 and 004512890 (browse-only territorial and county records) | Marriage, probate, church, census substitutes, territorial court/land records | Free |
| Ancestry.com (https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/census/) | U.S. Federal Census Collection | 1810 and 1820 federal census | Subscription |
| Fold3 (https://www.fold3.com/) | Military records | Creek War and War of 1812 service and pension records | Subscription |
| NARA (https://www.archives.gov/) | Federal records: passenger lists, naturalization, military pension files, GLO records | Federal-level records not in state archives | Free to search; copies may have fees |
| BLM GLO (https://glorecords.blm.gov) | Federal land patents, Alabama | Federal land grants from ca. 1799 onward | Free |
| Find A Grave (https://www.findagrave.com/) | Cemetery records | Burial locations where churchyard records do not survive | Free |

**Coverage of this survey:** The volume_search returned 2 digitized volumes for the 1780–1820 period, which is the complete result set (totalResults: 2). Both are browse-only.

### Physical repositories
| Repository | Holdings | Access method |
|---|---|---|
| Alabama Department of Archives and History (ADAH), Montgomery, AL | Territorial census records (1801, 1805, 1808, 1810); Mississippi Territory and Alabama Territory records; county records on microfilm; military records | In-person; online catalog at archives.alabama.gov |
| County probate courts (Washington County et al.) | Original deed books, probate files, marriage records from county formation | In-person or mail request |
| National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) | Federal land records, military service and pension files, passenger lists, naturalization records | In-person (Atlanta regional for Alabama); online via Ancestry/Fold3 |
| Mobile Municipal Archives, Mobile, AL | French colonial records on microfilm | In-person |
| Library of Congress, Washington, DC | Copies of Spanish colonial records (Archivo General de Indias) for the Mobile District | In-person; some digitized collections online |
| Archivo General de Indias, Seville, Spain | Original Spanish colonial records of the Mobile District, 1780–1813 | In-person or through formal request |
| Archives Nationales d'Outre-Mer, Aix-en-Provence, France | Original French colonial records (Mobile, 1702–1763) | In-person or formal request |

## Records NOT online
- Territorial census manuscripts (1801, 1805, 1808): physical only at ADAH.
- Washington County and other early county original deed and probate books (beyond the two browse-only FamilySearch volumes): in-person at the county courthouse or ADAH microfilm.
- Territorial tax lists: physical at ADAH.
- Spanish colonial church registers and land records: physical at Archivo General de Indias (Seville) and Library of Congress copies.
- French colonial records: physical at Archives Nationales d'Outre-Mer and on microfilm at Mobile Municipal Archives.
- Interior Alabama Baptist and Methodist circuit records: physical at ADAH or denominational archives if they survive at all.

## Known record losses
No tool result in this survey stated that a specific record set for this place and period was destroyed. The sparse digitization coverage reflects the extreme rarity of pre-1820 Alabama records generally, not confirmed losses. The Interior Alabama area had minimal civil infrastructure before 1813, so many vital events simply went unrecorded. A negative online search result is not evidence a record does not exist — it is more likely undigitized or held only in a physical repository.

## Research tips
- **Work backward through the jurisdictions.** Records follow the jurisdiction in force at the date of the event. For an event ca. 1800, search Mississippi Territory records first, then Washington County records; for 1817–1819, search Alabama Territory records. Only after 1819 do county Alabama state records apply.
- **The territorial census series is critical.** The Mississippi Territory censuses of 1801, 1805, 1808, and 1810 are the closest equivalent to a vital record for this period. They are held at ADAH, Montgomery (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Alabama_Genealogy#Territorial_Records).
- **The two browse-only FamilySearch volumes (004512889 and 004512890) must be examined page by page.** Neither has a name index or full-text search. Budget significant time to browse all 214 and 96 images respectively.
- **For the Mobile area, the colonial record trail is continuous but multi-archival.** French (Archives Nationales d'Outre-Mer, Aix-en-Provence; microfilm at Mobile Municipal Archives), Spanish (Archivo General de Indias, Seville; copies at Library of Congress), then American. Do not stop at the 1798 Mississippi Territory formation date if your ancestor was in Mobile (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Alabama_Genealogy#Colonial_Records).
- **Land records are the best substitute for missing vital records.** Federal patents (BLM GLO), territorial land grants, and county deed indexes all name individuals with approximate dates and often name neighboring landowners (useful for cluster research).
- **Tax lists fill census gaps.** County tax lists from Washington County (ca. 1800 onward) list heads of household annually and can track residence between census years.
- **FamilySearch Wiki Alabama-specific pages were unreachable during this survey.** All requests to Alabama_Genealogy, Alabama_Vital_Records, Alabama_Land_and_Property, Alabama_Church_Records, Alabama_Census, and Alabama_Probate_Records returned a generic fallback page. Re-run this locality guide or visit https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Alabama_Genealogy directly before relying on the absence of those pages.
